    Use Model Garden to discover, test, customize, and deploy Google proprietary and select OSS generative AI models and LLMs.

docs.title: Access control
docs.text:
To use the generative AI features on Vertex AI, principals such as users, groups, and service accounts must be granted the appropriate Identity and Access Management (IAM) role. You can use predefined roles for common use cases or create custom roles to grant a user-defined set of permissions.

This page describes the predefined roles and specific permissions applicable to generative AI features.

docs.title: Predefined roles
docs.text:
The simplest way to grant access to generative AI features is to assign a predefined role. The following table compares the most common predefined roles for Vertex AI.

Role Description Common Use Case Vertex AI Administrator (roles/aiplatform.admin) Provides full access to all Vertex AI resources, including generative AI features. For principals who need to manage all aspects of Vertex AI, including creating, deleting, and managing resources and permissions. Vertex AI User (roles/aiplatform.user) Provides permissions to use Vertex AI resources, but not to create or delete them. This includes making predictions with generative AI models. For developers, data scientists, and other users who need to use generative AI models and other Vertex AI features without having administrative control.

To learn more about all available Vertex AI IAM roles, see Vertex AI access control with IAM.

docs.title: Permissions for custom roles
docs.text:
If the predefined roles don't meet your needs, you can create a custom role with more granular permissions. The following table maps generative AI operations to the permissions required to perform them.

Operation Required Permissions Make prompt requests aiplatform.endpoints.predict Manage prompts in Vertex AI Studio (save, view, update, delete) aiplatform.datasets.createaiplatform.datasets.deleteaiplatform.datasets.getaiplatform.datasets.listaiplatform.datasets.update Tune a foundation model aiplatform.pipelineJobs.*aiplatform.customJobs.*aiplatform.datasets.exportaiplatform.datasets.getaiplatform.models.uploadaiplatform.models.getaiplatform.endpoints.createaiplatform.endpoints.getaiplatform.endpoints.deployaiplatform.metadataStores.getstorage.objects.createstorage.objects.getstorage.objects.liststorage.objects.update

To learn more about Vertex AI IAM permissions, see IAM permissions.

docs.title: Bounding box detection
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

With bounding box detection, you can identify and localize objects within images and video. By accurately identifying and delineating objects with bounding boxes, you can unlock a wide range of applications, such as object tracking, image search, and real-world scene analysis.

Key Benefits:

  • Simple: Integrate object detection capabilities into your applications with ease, regardless of your computer vision expertise.
  • Customizable: Produce bounding boxes based on custom instructions (for example, "I want to see bounding boxes of all the green objects in this image"), without having to train a custom model.

Technical Details:

  • Input: Your prompt and associated images or video frames.
  • Output: Bounding boxes in the [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] format. The top-left corner is the origin. The x and y axes go horizontally and vertically, respectively. Coordinate values are normalized to 0-1000 for every image.
  • Visualization: AI Studio users will see bounding boxes plotted within the UI. Vertex AI users should visualize their bounding boxes through custom visualization code.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text:
Follow the steps to detect bounding boxes

Before you begin

  1. Install the Python SDK for generative AI.

    pip install --upgrade google-genai

    To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

  2. Set environment variables to use the SDK with Vertex AI.

    # Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 1: Import libraries and define helpers

Import the necessary libraries and define a helper class and function to handle and visualize the bounding box data.

import requests

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import GenerateContentConfig, HttpOptions, Part, SafetySetting

from PIL import Image, ImageColor, ImageDraw

from pydantic import BaseModel

# Helper class to represent a bounding box
class BoundingBox(BaseModel):
    """
    Represents a bounding box with its 2D coordinates and associated label.

    Attributes:
        box_2d (list[int]): A list of integers representing the 2D coordinates of the bounding box,
                            typically in the format [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max].
        label (str): A string representing the label or class associated with the object within the bounding box.
    """

    box_2d: list[int]
    label: str

# Helper function to plot bounding boxes on an image
def plot_bounding_boxes(image_uri: str, bounding_boxes: list[BoundingBox]) -> None:
    """
    Plots bounding boxes on an image with markers for each a name, using PIL, normalized coordinates, and different colors.

    Args:
        img_path: The path to the image file.
        bounding_boxes: A list of bounding boxes containing the name of the object
        and their positions in normalized [y1 x1 y2 x2] format.
    """
    with Image.open(requests.get(image_uri, stream=True, timeout=10).raw) as im:
        width, height = im.size
        draw = ImageDraw.Draw(im)

        colors = list(ImageColor.colormap.keys())

        for i, bbox in enumerate(bounding_boxes):
            y1, x1, y2, x2 = bbox.box_2d
            abs_y1 = int(y1 / 1000 * height)
            abs_x1 = int(x1 / 1000 * width)
            abs_y2 = int(y2 / 1000 * height)
            abs_x2 = int(x2 / 1000 * width)

            color = colors[i % len(colors)]

            draw.rectangle(
                ((abs_x1, abs_y1), (abs_x2, abs_y2)), outline=color, width=4
            )
            if bbox.label:
                draw.text((abs_x1 + 8, abs_y1 + 6), bbox.label, fill=color)

        im.show()

Step 2: Initialize the client and configure the model

Initialize the client and configure the model parameters, including system instructions, safety settings, and the response schema. The response_schema ensures the output is structured according to the BoundingBox class.

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

config = GenerateContentConfig(
    system_instruction="""
    Return bounding boxes as an array with labels.
    Never return masks. Limit to 25 objects.
    If an object is present multiple times, give each object a unique label
    according to its distinct characteristics (colors, size, position, etc..).
    """,
    temperature=0.5,
    safety_settings=[
        SafetySetting(
            category="HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT",
            threshold="BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH",
        ),
    ],
    response_mime_type="application/json",
    response_schema=list[BoundingBox],  # Add BoundingBox class to the response schema
)

Step 3: Send the request and visualize the results

Prepare the request with an image and a text prompt. Send the request to the model, then print the structured response and use the helper function to plot the bounding boxes on the image.

image_uri = "https://storage.googleapis.com/generativeai-downloads/images/socks.jpg"

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents=[
        Part.from_uri(
            file_uri=image_uri,
            mime_type="image/jpeg",
        ),
        "Output the positions of the socks with a face. Label according to position in the image.",
    ],
    config=config,
)
print(response.text)
plot_bounding_boxes(image_uri, response.parsed)

Example response:

[
    {"box_2d": [36, 246, 380, 492], "label": "top left sock with face"},
    {"box_2d": [260, 663, 640, 917], "label": "top right sock with face"},
]

docs.title: Control access to Model Garden models
docs.text:
Vertex AI Model Garden's organization policy lets you centrally control which foundation models your users can access and what actions they can take. By default, any principal with permissions to use Vertex AI can use Model Garden to discover, customize, and deploy a wide variety of Google and third-party models.

Setting a Model Garden policy is useful when you need to enforce that only an approved set of models can be used in your environments. You can define a policy at the organization, folder, or project level to ensure users can only access the models you've approved.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
• Understand policy evaluation: Policies are evaluated hierarchically. When multiple policies apply to a resource, any explicit deny value overrides any allow value. For more information on how policies are merged and evaluated, see Understanding hierarchy evaluation in the Resource Manager documentation.
  • Required permissions: To manage organization policies, you need the Organization Policy Administrator (roles/orgpolicy.policyAdmin) IAM role.
  • Policy limitations:
    • The Model Garden organization policy applies only to models available in Model Garden. It does not apply to models registered in the Vertex AI Model Registry.
    • A single policy cannot exceed 500 total allowed and denied values.
    • Custom policies require you to specify each model individually. You cannot use wildcards or group models by publisher (for example, you can't deny all third-party models with a single rule).

docs.title: How to control access
docs.text: You can control access to Model Garden models by setting an organization policy. This policy can allow all models, deny all models, or define a custom list of allowed or denied models and actions.

docs.title: Choose a policy type
docs.text:
First, decide which type of policy enforcement best suits your governance needs.

Policy Type Description Use Case Allow all models This is the default behavior. All models and actions in Model Garden are accessible to users. Suitable for open development environments where no access restrictions are needed. Deny all models Blocks access to all models and actions in Model Garden. Useful for completely locking down Model Garden access while you define a more granular policy. Custom policy Allows you to specify a list of models and actions to either explicitly allow or deny. - Custom Allow: All models are denied except those on your list. - Custom Deny: All models are allowed except those on your list. Ideal for enforcing a curated list of approved models or blocking specific models that don't meet your compliance or cost requirements.

docs.title: Set a Model Garden access policy
docs.text:
The following workflow outlines the process for configuring a custom policy.

flowchart LR
    A[Choose a policy type] --> B[Identify the model and action];
    B --> C{Set the policy};
    C --> D[Using the Google Cloud console];
    C --> E[Using the gcloud CLI];

    click A "#choose-a-policy-type"
    click B "#step-1-identify-the-model-and-action"
    click C "#step-2-set-the-organization-policy"
    click D "#step-2-set-the-organization-policy"
    click E "#step-2-set-the-organization-policy"
Steps to set a Model Garden access policy

Step 1: Identify the model and action

To specify a model in a custom policy, you need its model ID and the action you want to control. The format is:

publishers/PUBLISHER/models/MODEL_NAME:ACTION

  • PUBLISHER: The publisher of the model (e.g., google, meta).
  • MODEL_NAME: The name of the model (e.g., gemini-1.5-flash-001).
  • ACTION: The specific action to allow or deny.

For example, to control prediction access for the Gemini 1.5 Flash model, you would use publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-flash-001:predict.

You can find the fully qualified model ID (publishers/PUBLISHER/models/MODEL_NAME) on the model card for each model in Model Garden. For a list of available models, see Explore AI models in Model Garden.

Available Actions

You can control the following actions for each model: * predict: Controls access to online and batch predictions for models with a managed API. * deploy: Controls one-click deployment for models that are deployed on Google Cloud. * tune: Controls access to model tuning features.

Step 2: Set the organization policy

You can set the policy using either the Google Cloud console or the gcloud CLI. The policy constraint for Model Garden is vertexai.allowedModels.

Google Cloud consolegcloud CLI
  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Organization policies page.
  2. Select the project, folder, or organization for which you want to set the policy.
  3. In the filter bar, search for the policy allowedModels.
  4. Click the Vertex AI Allowed Models policy to open the Policy details page.
  5. Click Edit to configure the policy.
  6. On the Edit policy page, select Customize.
  7. Choose a Policy enforcement option:
    • To allow a specific list, select Allow. Add policy values for each model and action you want to permit.
    • To deny a specific list, select Deny. Add policy values for each model and action you want to block.
  8. Click Save to apply the policy.

For more detailed instructions, see Setting a policy in the Google Cloud console.

  1. Create a YAML file that defines your policy. See the examples in the Policy examples section.
  2. Run the gcloud org-policies set command to apply the policy file to your organization, folder, or project.

To set the policy on an organization: 

gcloud org-policies set POLICY_FILE --organization=ORGANIZATION_ID

To set the policy on a folder: 

gcloud org-policies set POLICY_FILE --folder=FOLDER_ID

To set the policy on a project: 

gcloud org-policies set POLICY_FILE --project=PROJECT_ID
Replace POLICY_FILE with the path to your YAML policy file.

For more detailed instructions, see Setting a policy with the gcloud CLI.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with gcloud CLI commands or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Policy examples
docs.text:
The following examples show the YAML format used to set a policy with the gcloud CLI. Replace ORGANIZATION_ID with your Google Cloud organization ID. For more information, see Getting your organization ID.

Deny a set of models (allow all others)Allow a set of models (deny all others)

This policy denies specific actions on a list of models. All other models and actions are implicitly allowed.

name: organizations/ORGANIZATION_ID/policies/vertexai.allowedModels
spec:
  rules:
  - values:
      deniedValues:
      - publishers/meta/models/llama3:deploy
      - publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-flash-001:tune
      - publishers/hf-google/models/gemma-2b:deploy

This policy allows specific actions on a list of models. All other models and actions are implicitly denied.

name: organizations/ORGANIZATION_ID/policies/vertexai.allowedModels
spec:
  rules:
  - values:
      allowedValues:
      - publishers/meta/models/llama3:deploy
      - publishers/google/models/gemini-1.5-flash-001:tune
      - publishers/hf-google/models/gemma-2b:deploy

docs.title: Generative AI and data governance
docs.text: Google was the first in the industry to publish an AI/ML Privacy Commitment, which outlines our belief that customers should have the highest level of security and control over their data that is stored in the cloud. That commitment extends to Google Cloud's generative AI products. Google ensures that its teams are following these commitments through robust data governance practices, which include reviews of the data that Google Cloud uses in the development of its products. More details about how Google processes data can also be found in Google's Cloud Data Processing Addendum (CDPA).

docs.title: Training restriction
docs.text: As outlined in Section 17 "Training Restriction" in the Service Terms section of Service Specific Terms, Google won't use your data to train or fine-tune any AI/ML models without your prior permission or instruction. This applies to all managed models on Vertex AI, including GA and pre-GA models.

docs.title: Customer data retention and achieving zero data retention
docs.text:
By default, customer data is retained for limited periods in specific scenarios. To achieve zero data retention, you must take specific actions for each case. The following table summarizes the data retention scenarios for Google models on Vertex AI.

Scenario Data Retention Purpose & Duration How to Achieve Zero Data Retention Data caching for Google models Caches inputs to reduce latency for subsequent prompts. Data is stored for up to 24 hours. Disable data caching at the project level. See Manage data caching. Prompt logging for abuse monitoring Logs prompts to detect potential abuse and policy violations. Applies only to customers governed by the Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service without an Invoiced Cloud Billing account. Request an exception for abuse monitoring. See Abuse monitoring. Grounding with Google Search Stores prompts, contextual information, and generated output for 30 days to improve grounded results and for debugging. There is no way to disable this data storage if you use Grounding with Google Search. Session resumption for Gemini Live API If enabled by the user per API call, stores cached data (text, video, audio) for up to 24 hours to allow reconnection to a previous session. Do not enable the session resumption feature in the API request. See Live API.

docs.title: Manage data caching
docs.text:
You can manage data caching for your Google Cloud project by checking the current status and then enabling or disabling it as needed. The change applies to all Google Cloud regions for your project.

flowchart LR
    A[Get current cache setting] --> B{Decide action};
    B -- Need to disable --> C[Disable caching];
    B -- Need to enable --> D[Enable caching];

click A "#get-current-cache-setting"
click C "#disable-caching"
click D "#enable-caching"

For more information about the permissions required, see Vertex AI access control with IAM.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Get current cache settingDisable cachingEnable caching

Run the following command to determine if caching is enabled or disabled for a project. To run this command, a user must be granted one of the following roles: roles/aiplatform.viewer, roles/aiplatform.user, or roles/aiplatform.admin.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
# Setup project_id
$ gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID

# GetCacheConfig
$ curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig

# Response if caching is enabled (caching is enabled by default).
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig"
}

# Response if caching is disabled.
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig"
  "disableCache": true
}

Run the following curl command to disable caching for a Google Cloud project. To run this command, a user must be granted the Vertex AI Administrator role, roles/aiplatform.admin.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
# Setup project_id
$ gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID

# Opt-out of caching.
$ curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig -d '{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig",
  "disableCache": true
}'

# Response.
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig/operations/${OPERATION_ID}",
  "done": true,
  "response": {
    "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.protobuf.Empty"
  }
}

If you previously disabled caching and want to re-enable it, run the following curl command. To run this command, a user must be granted the Vertex AI Administrator role, roles/aiplatform.admin.

PROJECT_ID=PROJECT_ID
LOCATION_ID="us-central1"
# Setup project_id
$ gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID

# Opt in to caching.
$ curl -X PATCH     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig -d '{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig",
  "disableCache": false
}'

# Response.
{
  "name": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/projects/PROJECT_ID/cacheConfig/operations/${OPERATION_NUMBER}",
  "done": true,
  "response": {
    "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.protobuf.Empty"
  }
}

docs.title: Dynamic shared quota (DSQ)
docs.text: Dynamic shared quota (DSQ) serves your pay-as-you-go (PayGo) requests with greater flexibility to adapt to your workload needs without you having to manage quotas and quota increase requests (QIR). With DSQ, there are no predefined quota limits on your usage. Instead, DSQ provides access to a large, shared pool of resources, dynamically allocated based on real-time availability and demand across all customers of that model. When more customers are active, each customer gets a lower amount of throughput. Similarly, if there are fewer active customers, each customer might get higher throughput.

docs.title: When to use Dynamic Shared Quota
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers two main ways to manage throughput for generative AI models: Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) and Provisioned Throughput. DSQ is ideal for applications with variable traffic, while Provisioned Throughput is designed for applications requiring stable performance and high availability.

Use this comparison to decide which option is best for your workload.

Feature Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) Provisioned Throughput Cost Model Pay-as-you-go (PayGo). You only pay for what you use. Billed per hour for a reserved number of processing units. Performance Throughput is dynamic and depends on shared resource availability and overall demand. Stable, predictable, and guaranteed throughput. Use Case Development, testing, and applications with intermittent or unpredictable traffic patterns. Production-grade applications requiring high availability and consistent performance. Availability Access to a large, shared pool of resources. Subject to resource contention during peak demand, which can result in 429 errors. Reserved capacity ensures high availability and protects against "noisy neighbor" issues.

To learn more about Provisioned Throughput, see the Provisioned Throughput overview.

docs.text:

docs.title: How DSQ works
docs.text:
Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) adapts to your traffic patterns and needs and minimizes usage friction. Your project's access to resources under DSQ is not capped by a predefined limit. Instead, it's determined by the overall capacity of the shared pool and the current collective demand from all customers. This model is designed to offer significant flexibility, allowing your workloads to burst and consume more resources when available. Conversely, it also allows all customers of the shared pool to have a chance to access resources when available without requiring per-customer quota configuration.

To ensure a fair and stable experience for all users in the shared resource environment, DSQ intelligently manages how requests are handled, especially during periods of very high demand from isolated sources. Rather than a fixed cap, DSQ employs a dynamic prioritization approach. This means that while the system is designed to accommodate bursts, unusually large and rapid spikes in traffic from a single source might be handled with a different priority than more consistent, steady traffic. This sophisticated management ensures that broad user activity and regular workloads are protected from transient, extreme spikes, promoting overall system stability and equitable access.

Gemini requests with multi-modal inputs are subject to the corresponding system rate limits that include image, audio, video, and document.

docs.title: Understanding Resource Exhaustion 429 errors under DSQ
docs.text:
Encountering a 'resource exhausted' (429) error can be frustrating. With DSQ, this error does not mean you have hit a specific quota limit on your project. Instead, these errors indicate that the shared pool of resources for a specific model in a specific region is experiencing extremely high demand from many users simultaneously. Think of it like trying to get on a very popular train during peak rush hour. There isn't a 'ticket limit' specifically for you, but the train itself might be momentarily full. It's a temporary state of contention for resources, not a fixed limit imposed on your project.

DSQ constantly works to manage and distribute the available capacity fairly and efficiently. When you receive a 429 error, it means instantaneous demand has outstripped the available supply in that shared pool. Unlike a hard quota where you'd be blocked even if resources were idle, DSQ aims to give you access whenever resources are free. The exhaustion error is a reflection of the entire system's current load, not a ceiling on your account.

We recommend implementing retry mechanisms, as availability in this dynamic environment can change quickly. For more tactics on handling Resource Exhaustion errors, see Error code 429.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide for Vertex AI.

docs.title: Enable Data Access audit logs
docs.text:
To monitor who is accessing your Vertex AI resources and how they are being used, you can enable Data Access audit logs. These logs help you track API calls that read configuration or metadata, as well as calls that read or write user-provided data. Enabling these logs is essential for security auditing, tracking usage patterns, and troubleshooting issues.

Data Access audit logs for Vertex AI are categorized into three types:

Log Type Description Admin Read Records operations that read metadata or configuration information. For example, getting the details of a model endpoint. Data Read Records operations that read user-provided data. For example, making a prediction request to an endpoint. Data Write Records operations that write user-provided data. For example, uploading a dataset.

These logs are sent to Cloud Logging, where you can view, query, and set up alerts. For more detailed information about audit logging in Vertex AI, see Vertex AI audit logging information.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Prerequisites

  • To enable or disable Data Access audit logs, you need a role with the logging.configWriter permission, such as the Logging Config Writer (roles/logging.configWriter) IAM role.

  • To view the data_access log stream after it's enabled, you need a role with the logging.privateLogViewer permission, such as the Private Logs Viewer (roles/logging.privateLogViewer) IAM role.

  • Note that enabling Data Access audit logs might affect your Cloud Logging costs. For more information, see Logging pricing.

docs.title: Enable Data Access audit logs workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Go to Audit Logs] --> B[Select Vertex AI service] --> C[Enable log types] --> D[Save configuration]

    click A "#navigate-to-audit-logs"
    click B "#select-vertex-ai"
    click C "#enable-log-types"

docs.title: Steps to enable Data Access audit logs
docs.text:
The following steps guide you through enabling Data Access audit logs for Vertex AI in the Google Cloud console.

Step-by-step guide

1. Navigate to the Audit Logs page

In the Google Cloud console, go to the IAM & Admin > Audit Logs page.

Go to Audit Logs

2. Select the Vertex AI service

In the filter bar at the top of the services list, enter Vertex AI. Click on the Vertex AI API result to open its audit logging configuration.

3. Enable the desired log types

In the Log Types tab, select the checkboxes for the Data Access audit log types you want to enable: - Admin Read: To log access to metadata and configuration. - Data Read: To log access to user data. - Data Write: To log modifications to user data.

4. Save the configuration

Click Save. The selected log types are now enabled for your project.

docs.title: View audit logs
docs.text:
After you enable Data Access audit logs, they are sent to Cloud Logging. You can view them using the Logs Explorer.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Logging > Logs Explorer page.

    Go to Logs Explorer

  2. In the Query pane, build a query to filter for the logs you want to see. For example, to view all Data Access logs for Vertex AI, you can use the following query:

    resource.type="audited_resource"
resource.labels.service="aiplatform.googleapis.com"
logName:"data_access"

  3. Click Run query to see the results.

docs.title: Gemini 2.0 general FAQ
docs.text:
Help! The model I'm using isn't available anymore!

If your application recently started showing errors related to an unavailable Palm2, Gemini 1.0, or Gemini 1.5-001 model, this document covers how you can transition to a supported model.

Google regularly releases new and improved AI models. To make way for these advancements, older models are retired (or deprecated). We provide notice when deprecating a model and a transition window before access to the model is terminated, but we understand it can still cause interruptions.

Here are two options for updating your model:

  1. The quickest way to resolve the error is usually to switch your application code to one of the supported models. Test all critical features to make sure everything works as expected, then launch the change like you normally would.
  2. If you have a bit more time, consider our step-by-step migration process. This walks you through upgrading to the latest Gemini SDK and includes best practices to help minimize any risks during the switch. You can use this approach to minimize any potential risks of model migration and make sure that you are using the new model in an optimal way.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Which Gemini 2.0 models are available on Vertex AI as of February 25, 2025?

The following 2.0 models are available as of February 25, 2025:

  • Gemini 2.0 Flash (GA)
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite (GA)
  • Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking (Experimental)
  • Gemini 2.5 Pro (Experimental)
How do the Gemini 2.0 models compare to the 1.5 generation?

The Gemini 2.0 models feature the following upgrades over our 1.5 models:

  • Improved multilingual capabilities: Gemini 2.0 models show strong advancements in multilingual understanding, with increased scores in the Global MMLU (Lite) benchmark.
  • Significant gains in reasoning and knowledge factuality: Gemini 2.5 Pro shows substantial improvements in GPQA (domain expert reasoning) and SimpleQA (world knowledge factuality) indicating enhanced ability to understand and provide accurate information.
  • Enhanced mathematical problem-solving: Both Gemini 2.0 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Pro demonstrate notable progress in handling complex mathematical problems, as evidenced by the MATH and HiddenMath benchmarks.

The following table shows the comparison between our 2.0 models:

Model name Description Upgrade path for Gemini 2.5 Pro Strongest model quality (especially for code and world knowledge), with a 2M token-long context window Gemini 1.5 Pro users who want better quality, or who are particularly invested in long context and code Gemini 2.0 Flash Workhorse model for all daily tasks and features enhanced performance and supports real-time Live API
  • Gemini 1.5 Flash users who want a model with significantly better quality that's slightly slower
  • Gemini 1.5 Pro users who want slightly better quality and real-time latency
Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite Our most cost effective offering to support high throughput
  • Gemini 1.5 Flash users who want better quality for the same price and speed
  • Customers looking for the fastest model in the Gemini 2.0 family

To see all benchmark capabilities for Gemini 2.0, visit the Google DeepMind documentation.

How do I migrate Gemini on Google AI Studio to Vertex AI Studio?

Migrating to Google Cloud's Vertex AI platform offers a suite of MLOps tools that streamline the usage, deployment, and monitoring of AI models for efficiency and reliability. To migrate your work to Vertex AI, import and upload your existing data to Vertex AI Studio and use the Gemini API with Vertex AI.

For more information, see Migrate from Gemini on Google AI to Vertex AI.

How does Gemini 2.0 image generation compare to Imagen 3?

While the experimental version of Gemini 2.0 Flash supports image generation, Gemini 2.0 does not currently support image generation in our generally available models. The experimental version of Gemini 2.0 Flash shouldn't be used in production-level code.

If you need image generation in production code, use Imagen 3. This powerful model offers high-quality images, low-latency generation, and flexible editing options.

Does Gemini 2.0 in Vertex AI support compositional function calling?

Compositional function calling is only available in Google AI Studio.

What locations are supported for Gemini 2.0?

For the full list of locations that are supported for Gemini 2.0 models, see Locations.

What are the default quotas for Gemini 2.0?

Gemini 2.0 Flash and Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite use dynamic shared quota and have no default quota.

Gemini 2.5 Pro is an experimental model and has a 10 queries per minute (QPM) limit.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
Why does my quota usage show as 0% percent on API dashboard when I'm sending requests?

For Gemini models on Vertex, we use a Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) system. This innovative approach automatically manages capacity across all users in a region, ensuring optimal performance without the need for manual quota adjustments or requests. As a result, you won't see traditional quota usage displayed in the Quotas & System Limits tab. Your project will automatically receive the necessary resources based on real-time availability.

Use the Vertex AI Model Garden (Monitoring) dashboard to monitor usage.

docs.title: Provisioned Throughput
Getting help
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers several ways to get support depending on your needs. Use the following table to determine the best option for your situation.

Support option Best for... Ask a question on the Google Cloud Community. Use the Vertex AI Platform tag.
