docs.title: Render the Google Maps contextual widget
docs.text:
Rendering the Google Maps contextual widget is required as part of using Grounding with Google Maps in Vertex AI. In any response that is grounded with Google Maps, there is a corresponding googleMapsWidgetContextToken that is used to render the contextual widget in close proximity to the generated response.

  "googleMapsWidgetContextToken": "widgetcontent/AcBXPQdpWQWbap9H-OH8sEKmOXxmEKAYvff0tvthhneMQC3VrqWCjpnPBl4-Id98FGiA_S_t8aeAeJj0T6JkWFX56Bil8oBSR0W8JH3C_RSYLbTjxKdpxc9yNn6JcZTtolIRZon9xi6WpNGuSyjcIxWu2S0hwpasNOpUlWrG1RxVCB4WD1fsz_pwR236mG36lMxevXTQ_JnfdYNuQwQ4Lc3vn...<snip>...
  Ts5VJE_b3IC5eE_6wez0nh61r7foTUZpP7BXMwxR-7Wyfcj6x1v6mIWsFGr1o0p_HSAMNqWPg-aFVnkPLhAkOR6MaNZOfezTva-gxHlu7z_haFvYxcUE1qfNVQ",

Your page that displays the widget must use the alpha version of the Google Maps JS API. For more information, see Load the Maps JavaScript API.

You must use the API key that was enabled for Grounding with Google Maps in Vertex AI to load the Google Maps JS API.

Example: Create a widget using HTML

This code sample demonstrates how to create a widget using HTML.

  <body>
    <gmp-place-contextual id="widget"></gmp-place-contextual>
  </body>
Example: Update the context token with JavaScript

In your Javascript, use the following method to update the context token:

function updateWidget(contextToken) {
  let widget = document.querySelector('#widget');
  widget.contextToken = contextToken;
}
Example: Create a widget dynamically with JavaScript

You can also create a widget dynamically with the following code:

async function createWidget(contextToken) {
  await google.maps.importLibrary('places');
  let widgetContainer = document.querySelector('#wc');  // a div that contains the widget
  const placeContextualElement = new
      google.maps.places.PlaceContextualElement({ contextToken });
  widgetContainer.appendChild(placeContextualElement);
}
Example: Configure widget layout with HTML

This HTML code sample demonstrates how to use configuration options to toggle between two different layouts (compact or vertical).

    <gmp-place-contextual id="widget">
      <gmp-place-contextual-list-config layout="compact">
      </gmp-place-contextual-list-config>
    </gmp-place-contextual>
Example: Disable the map with HTML

This HTML code sample demonstrates how to disable the map.

    <gmp-place-contextual id="widget">
      <gmp-place-contextual-list-config map-hidden>
      </gmp-place-contextual-list-config>
    </gmp-place-contextual>
Example: Configure widget layout and map visibility with JavaScript

This JavaScript code sample demonstrates how to specify a compact layout and how to hide the map.

  const widgetConfig = new google.maps.places.PlaceContextualListConfigElement({
    layout: 'compact',
    mapHidden: true
  });
  widget.appendChild(widgetConfig);

docs.title: Grounding with Google Search
docs.text:
This page explains how to ground a model's responses using Google Search, which uses publicly available web data. Grounding helps ensure responses are based on the latest and most accurate information available on the internet.

If you want to connect your model with world knowledge, a wide range of topics, or up-to-date information, use grounding with Google Search.

Important: If you receive Google Search suggestions with a response, that response is a "Grounded Result" subject to the Grounding with Google Search terms in the Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. To use Google Search suggestions, see Use Google Search suggestions.

Note for web publishers: Grounding with Google Search on Vertex AI does not use web pages for grounding that have disallowed Google-Extended. Web publishers can manage inclusion in Google-Extended with a robots.txt file.

To learn more about model grounding in Vertex AI, see the Grounding overview.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Using Google Search as a tool enables complex prompts and workflows that require planning, reasoning, and up-to-date information. Key benefits include:

  • Grounding responses to the latest and most accurate information.
  • Retrieving and analyzing artifacts from the web.
  • Finding relevant images, videos, or other media to assist in multimodal reasoning.
  • Performing coding, technical troubleshooting, and other specialized tasks.
  • Finding region-specific information or assisting in content translation.
  • Finding relevant websites for browsing.

docs.title: Ground your model with Google Search
docs.text:
You can ground a model with publicly available web data using the Vertex AI Studio, the Generative AI SDKs, or the REST API.

The following diagram shows the workflow for grounding a model in the Vertex AI Studio.

flowchart LR
    A[Navigate to Vertex AI Studio] --> B[Enable grounding and set source] --> C[Enter prompt and submit]

click A "#navigate-to-vertex-ai-studio"
click B "#enable-grounding-and-set-source"
click C "#enter-prompt-and-submit"
Before you begin
  • To use grounding with Google Search, you must enable Google Search Suggestions. For more information, see Use Google Search suggestions.
  • For ideal results, use a temperature of 1.0. To learn more about setting this configuration, see the Gemini API request body from the model reference.
  • Grounding with Google Search has a limit of one million queries per day. If you require more queries, contact Google Cloud support for assistance.
ConsolePythonGoREST API

To use grounding with Google Search in the Vertex AI Studio, follow these steps:

1. Navigate to Vertex AI Studio

  • In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio page. Go to Vertex AI Studio
  • Click the Freeform tab.

2. Enable grounding and set the source

  • In the side panel, click the Ground model responses toggle.
  • Click Customize and set Google Search as the source.

3. Enter your prompt and submit

  • Enter your prompt in the text box and click Submit.

Your prompt responses are now grounded to Google Search.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Install the SDK

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

pip install --upgrade google-genai

Set environment variables

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    GenerateContentConfig,
    GoogleSearch,
    HttpOptions,
    Tool,
)

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="When is the next total solar eclipse in the United States?",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[

print(response.text)

Install the SDK

Learn how to install or update the Generative AI SDK for Go. To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

Set environment variables

Example

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"

    genai "google.golang.org/genai"
)

// generateWithGoogleSearch shows how to generate text using Google Search.
func generateWithGoogleSearch(w io.Writer) error {
    ctx := context.Background()

    client, err := genai.NewClient(ctx, &genai.ClientConfig{
        HTTPOptions: genai.HTTPOptions{APIVersion: "v1"},
    })
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to create genai client: %w", err)
    }

    modelName := "gemini-2.0-flash-001"
    contents := []*genai.Content{
        {Parts: []*genai.Part{
            {Text: "When is the next total solar eclipse in the United States?"},
        }},
    }
    config := &genai.GenerateContentConfig{
        Tools: []*genai.Tool{
            {GoogleSearch: &genai.GoogleSearch{}},
        },
    }

    resp, err := client.Models.GenerateContent(ctx, modelName, contents, config)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate content: %w", err)
    }

    respText, err := resp.Text()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to convert model response to text: %w", err)
    }
    fmt.Fprintln(w, respText)

    // Example response:
    // The next total solar eclipse in the United States will occur on March 30, 2033, but it will only ...

    return nil
}

docs.title: Grounding support
docs.text:
Displaying grounding support is recommended because it helps you validate responses from the publishers and provides avenues for further learning.

Grounding support for responses from Google Search sources should be shown both inline and in aggregate. The following image provides a suggestion for how to display this information.

Grounding support examples.

docs.title: Use of alternative search engine options
docs.text: A customer's use of Grounding with Google Search does not prevent the customer from offering alternative search engine options, making alternative search options the default for customer applications, or displaying their own or third-party search suggestions or search results in customer applications. However, any such non-Google Search services or associated results must be displayed separately from the Grounded Results and Search Suggestions and can't reasonably be attributed to, or confused with, results provided by Google.

docs.title: Grounding with Vertex AI Search
docs.text:
This page explains how you can ground model responses by using your data from Vertex AI Search. Grounding connects a model to your enterprise data to provide responses that are more accurate, specific, and relevant. This process is also known as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

Grounding with your data supports a maximum of 10 Vertex AI Search data sources and can be combined with Grounding with Google Search.

  • Gemini 2.0 Flash with Live API

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Vertex AI Search data store
docs.text:
To ground your model, you need a data store in Vertex AI Search. You can create a data store from your website content or from documents stored in Cloud Storage. Use the following table to decide which data source is right for you.

Feature Website data Documents Use Case Grounding on publicly available information from specific websites. Grounding on proprietary or unstructured documents (PDF, HTML, TXT, etc.) stored in Cloud Storage. Data Source URLs of websites to include or exclude. Files in a Cloud Storage bucket. Indexing Advanced website indexing crawls and processes the content from the specified URLs. Documents are parsed, chunked, and indexed. Website dataDocuments

  1. Open the Create Data Store page in the Google Cloud console.

  2. In the Website Content box, click Select. The Specify the websites for your data store pane is displayed.

  3. If Advanced website indexing isn't checked, select the Advanced website indexing checkbox to turn it on. The Configure your data store pane is displayed.

  4. In the Specify URL patterns to index section, do the following:

    • Add URLs for Sites to include.
    • Optional: Add URLs for Sites to exclude.

  5. Click Continue.

  6. In the Configure your data store pane:

    1. Select a value from the Location of your data store list.
    2. Enter a name in the Your data store name field. The ID is generated automatically. You will use this ID when you generate grounded responses.
    3. Click Create.

  1. Open the Create Data Store page in the Google Cloud console.

  2. In the Cloud Storage box, click Select. The Import data from Cloud Storage pane is displayed.

  3. In the Unstructured documents (PDF, HTML, TXT and more) section, select Unstructured documents (PDF, HTML, TXT and more).

  4. Select a Synchronization frequency option.

  5. Select a Select a folder or a file you want to import option, and enter the path in the field.

  6. Click Continue. The Configure your data store pane is displayed.

  7. In the Configure your data store pane:

    1. Select a value from the Location of your data store list.
    2. Enter a name in the Your data store name field. The ID is generated automatically.
    3. To select parsing and chunking options for your documents, expand the Document Processing Options section. For more information about different parsers, see Parse documents.
    4. Click Create.

docs.title: Step 2: Generate grounded responses
docs.text:
After you create your data store, you can use it to ground model responses. You can ground a model with up to 10 data stores.

First, you need your data store ID. If you don't know your data store ID, follow these steps:

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the AI Applications page and in the navigation menu, click Data stores.

    Go to the Data stores page

  2. Click the name of your data store.

  3. On the Data page for your data store, get the data store ID.

Now, use one of the following methods to generate a grounded response.

ConsolePythonREST API

To ground your model output using Vertex AI Studio in the Google Cloud console, follow these steps:

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio Freeform page.

    Go to Freeform

  2. To turn on grounding, click the Grounding: your data toggle.

  3. Click Customize.

    1. Select Vertex AI Search as your source.

    2. Using this path format, replace project_id and data_store_id with your information:

      projects/project_id/locations/global/collections/default_collection/dataStores/data_store_id

  4. Click Save.

  5. Enter your prompt in the text box, and click Submit.

Your prompt responses are now grounded to your Vertex AI Search data store.

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

docs.title: Step 3: Understand your response
docs.text:
The API response includes the LLM-generated text, called a candidate. If your model prompt successfully grounds to your data source, the response includes grounding metadata that identifies the parts of the response derived from your data. However, this metadata might not be provided if source relevance is low or information is incomplete.

The following is a breakdown of the output data:

  • Role: Indicates the sender of the grounded answer. Because the response always contains grounded text, the role is always model.
  • Text: The grounded answer generated by the LLM.
  • Grounding metadata: Information about the grounding source, which contains the following elements:
    • Grounding chunks: A list of results from your data store that support the answer.
    • Grounding supports: Information about a specific claim within the answer that can be used to show citations:
      • Segment: The part of the model's answer that is substantiated by a grounding chunk.
      • Grounding chunk index: The index of the grounding chunks in the groundingChunks list that corresponds to this claim.
      • Confidence scores: A number from 0 to 1 that indicates how grounded the claim is in the provided set of grounding chunks. Not available for Gemini 2.5 and later.

docs.title: Grounding with your search API
docs.text:
You can connect Gemini to your external data sources by grounding with your search API. This lets you use any search service as a grounding source for Gemini, which helps to ensure that responses are based on the latest and most relevant information from your systems. This is particularly useful for enterprise-specific data that isn't publicly available.

This page explains how to configure and use grounding using any search API with Gemini.

docs.title: Choose your approach
docs.text:
Before you begin, decide whether you will use an existing, compatible API endpoint or set up a new one.

Approach Description Best for... Use a compatible endpoint Configure Gemini to call your existing search API directly. You already have a search API that meets the required schema and can be secured with an API key. Set up a new search API endpoint Create a new, secure API endpoint using Cloud Functions and API Gateway to wrap your data source. You need to build a new API to interface with your data source (e.g., a database or internal search engine) and make it compatible with Gemini.

docs.title: How grounding with your search API works
docs.text:
When you ground with your search API, Gemini can query an external API endpoint that you provide. This allows Gemini to use your custom search functionality as a tool to enhance its responses. It enables more dynamic and context-aware interactions, as the model can seek out information from your specified data sources when needed.

During a generation request, Gemini can make a call to the external API endpoint with a search query. Your API should then return relevant data snippets. Gemini uses these snippets as a source of truth to generate a more accurate and grounded response.

You can combine grounding using your search API with other grounding sources like Google Search. A generation request supports up to 10 grounding sources and multi-tool queries where Gemini can take advantage of different information sources to generate the best possible answer.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
The following models support grounding with your API:

  • Gemini 1.5 Pro
  • Gemini 1.5 Flash
  • Gemini 1.0 Pro

For more information, see Gemini models.

docs.title: Search API requirements
docs.text: To use your existing search infrastructure with Gemini, your API endpoint must meet the following requirements.

docs.title: API schema
docs.text:
• HTTP method: POST
  • Request Body (from Gemini to your API): 
    {
  "query": "the user's search query string"
}
  • Response body (from your API to Gemini): A JSON array of objects. Each object represents a search result and must contain snippet and uri fields. 
    [
  {
    "snippet": "A text snippet containing the answer or relevant information.",
    "uri": "A URI/URL linking to the source of the information, or a relevant identifier."
  },
  {
    "snippet": "Another piece of information.",
    "uri": "https://example.com/another-source"
  }
]
    If no results are found, your API endpoint should return an empty array [].

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Grounding with your search API supports the use of an API key to secure your API endpoint. Gemini sends this API key as a query parameter named key.

docs.title: Considerations for your search API
docs.text:
Review the following considerations to help you choose your search API:

  • Snippet quality: The snippet text returned by your API is crucial. It should be concise yet informative enough for Gemini to use as a factual basis for its response.
  • Latency: Your search API should respond quickly. High latency in your API increases the overall response time from Gemini.
  • Error handling: Implement robust error handling in your Cloud Function or search API. If your API frequently errors or times out, it negatively impacts Gemini's ability to generate grounded responses.
Use a compatible endpointSet up a new search API endpoint

If you already have an API endpoint that meets the schema and authentication requirements, you can directly configure it in your Gemini API calls.

If you don't have a compatible API endpoint, this guide walks you through setting one up using Cloud Functions and API Gateway.

flowchart LR
    A[Step 1: Create Cloud Function] --> B[Step 2: Secure with API Gateway]
    B --> C[Step 3: Create and Restrict API Key]

click A "#step-1-create-the-cloud-function"
click B "#step-2-secure-with-api-gateway"
click C "#step-3-create-and-restrict-an-api-key"
Before you begin
  1. Ensure that the Vertex AI API is enabled in your Google Cloud project.
  2. Make sure you have the Google Cloud CLI installed and initialized.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Step 1: Create the Cloud Function

A Cloud Function can act as an intermediary that receives queries from Gemini, issues appropriate queries to your existing search infrastructure (such as a database, internal search engine, or vector search), and then formats the results in the schema Gemini understands. For more information, see the Cloud Functions documentation.

This example uses a hardcoded product list for demonstration. You'll need to replace the data retrieval logic with calls to your actual search system.

1. Create the function files

  • main.py 

    import functions_framework
import json
from flask import jsonify

@functions_framework.http
def custom_search_wrapper_minimal(request):
    """
    HTTP Cloud Function to provide a minimal, fixed response for Gemini grounding.
    """
    if request.method != 'POST':
        return 'Only POST requests are accepted', 405

    request_json = request.get_json(silent=True)

    if not request_json or 'query' not in request_json:
        return jsonify({"error": "Invalid request. JSON body with 'query' field is required."}), 400

    user_query = request_json['query']
    print(f"Received query: '{user_query}'. Responding with fixed data.")

    # --- FIXED RESPONSE ---
    # This is a hardcoded response. In a real scenario, you would
    # use the 'user_query' to fetch relevant data.
    fixed_results = [
        {
            "snippet": "This is a fixed snippet from your custom Search API. The original query was: " + user_query,
            "uri": "https://example.com/docs/fixed-test-data"
        },
        {
            "snippet": "Another piece of fixed information to demonstrate the list format.",
            "uri": "https://example.com/another-fixed-source"
        }
    ]
    # --- END OF FIXED RESPONSE ---

    return jsonify(fixed_results)

  • requirements.txt 

    functions-framework>=3.0.0
Flask>=2.0.0

2. Deploy the function

Navigate to the directory containing main.py and requirements.txt and run the following command. Replace YOUR_REGION with your chosen Google Cloud region (e.g., us-central1).

gcloud functions deploy custom_search_wrapper \
  --runtime python311 \
  --trigger-http \
  --entry-point custom_search_wrapper_minimal \
  --region YOUR_REGION \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --gen2
* --allow-unauthenticated is specified because API Gateway will handle authentication.

Important: After deployment, note the trigger URL, which has a format of https://....run.app. You will use this URL in the next step.

Step 2: Secure with API Gateway

API Gateway provides a secure, managed entry point to your Cloud Function and lets you enforce API key authentication. For more information, see the API Gateway documentation.

1. Create an OpenAPI specification

Create a file named openapi-spec.yaml. This file defines how API Gateway exposes your Cloud Function. Replace YOUR_CLOUD_FUNCTION_TRIGGER_URL with the trigger URL you noted in the previous step.

swagger: '2.0'
info:
  title: Custom Search API for Gemini Grounding
  description: Wraps an internal search function, secured by API Key for Gemini.
  version: 1.0.0
schemes:
  - https
produces:
  - application/json
consumes:
  - application/json
paths:
  /v0/search:
    post:
      summary: Custom search endpoint for Gemini
      operationId: customSearchForGemini
      x-google-backend:
        address: YOUR_CLOUD_FUNCTION_TRIGGER_URL # Replace with your Cloud Function trigger URL
      parameters:
        - name: body
          in: body
          required: true
          schema:
            type: object
            properties:
              query:
                type: string
      security:
        - api_key_query: []
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Search results
          schema:
            type: array
            items:
              type: object
              properties:
                snippet:
                  type: string
                uri:
                  type: string
        '400':
          description: Invalid request
        '401':
          description: Unauthorized (Missing or invalid API key)
        '500':
          description: Internal server error
securityDefinitions:
  api_key_query:
    type: apiKey
    name: key # Gemini will send its API key using this query parameter name
    in: query

2. Deploy API Gateway

Execute the following gcloud CLI commands, replacing YOUR_PROJECT_ID and YOUR_REGION.

# 1. Create an API
gcloud api-gateway apis create custom-search-gemini-api --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

# 2. Create an API Config from your OpenAPI spec
gcloud api-gateway api-configs create v1 \
  --api=custom-search-gemini-api \
  --openapi-spec=openapi-spec.yaml \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --display-name="Version 1"

# 3. Create a Gateway
gcloud api-gateway gateways create custom-search-gateway \
  --api=custom-search-gemini-api \
  --api-config=v1 \
  --location=YOUR_REGION \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

After deployment, the hostname (gateway URL) has the format https://custom-search-gateway-UNIQUE_ID.nw.gateway.dev. You can use this to construct the full endpoint URL for Gemini (e.g., https://custom-search-gateway-UNIQUE_ID.nw.gateway.dev/v0/search).

Step 3: Create and restrict an API key

You must create an API key that Gemini will use to access your API Gateway endpoint. For more information, see Managing API keys.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the APIs & Services > Credentials page. Go to Credentials
  2. Click Create credentials and select API key.
  3. Click Show key and copy the generated API key. Store the key in a secure location. This is the key you will provide to Gemini.
  4. Click Edit API key or click the key name to open the key's settings.
  5. In the API restrictions section, do the following:
    1. Select the Restrict key option.
    2. In the dropdown menu, select your API Gateway managed service. It should be named after your API, such as Custom Search API for Gemini Grounding API.
    3. If the key isn't included or if you intend to manage the gateway with the API using this key, ensure that the API Gateway API (apigateway.googleapis.com) is also selected. For grounding, the key needs access to your specific API service hosted by API Gateway. Note: It is a best practice to use a separate key or service account for management tasks.
  6. Click Save.

Your API Gateway endpoint is now secured. When you use the endpoint, you must pass the API key as a query parameter. For example: https://custom-search-gateway-UNIQUE_ID.nw.gateway.dev/v0/search?key=YOUR_GENERATED_API_KEY

docs.title: Configure the externalApi tool
docs.text:
When making a request to the Gemini API, include the tools parameter with a retrieval tool configured for the externalApi. Key fields include the following:

  • api_spec:"SIMPLE_SEARCH": This tells Gemini to use the predefined input and output schema.
  • endpoint: The full URL to your API Gateway endpoint, such as https://YOUR_GATEWAY_HOSTNAME/v0/search.
  • apiAuth.apiKeyConfig.apiKeyString: The API key that Gemini uses to authenticate with your API. Gemini appends this key as ?key=<YOUR_API_KEY> to the endpoint URL.

docs.title: Send the request
docs.text:
Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: The region to process the request, such as us-central1.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • MODEL_ID: The model ID of a compatible Gemini model, such as gemini-1.0-pro-002.
  • USER_PROMPT: The text instructions to include in the prompt.
  • EXTERNAL_API_ENDPOINT: The full URL to your secured API Gateway endpoint that Gemini calls, such as https://YOUR_GATEWAY_HOSTNAME/v0/search. This endpoint must adhere to the specified API schema.
  • EXTERNAL_API_KEY: The API key you generated and configured for your API Gateway. Gemini uses this key to authenticate with your endpoint.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent

Request JSON body:

{
  "contents": [{
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [{
          "text": "USER_PROMPT"
      }]
  }],
  "tools": [{
      "retrieval": {
        "externalApi": {
          "api_spec": "SIMPLE_SEARCH",
          "endpoint": "EXTERNAL_API_ENDPOINT",
          "apiAuth": {
            "apiKeyConfig": {
              "apiKeyString": "EXTERNAL_API_KEY"
            }
          }
        }
      }
  }]
}

To send your request, choose one of the following options:

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

cURLPowerShell

The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d @request.json \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_ID:generateContent"

The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
  -Method POST `

docs.text: • Grounding with Google Search.

docs.title: Grounding overview
docs.text:
In generative AI, grounding is the process of connecting a model's responses to verifiable sources of information. For example, if you ask a model about your company's latest product features, grounding ensures the model bases its answer on your internal product documentation rather than on public, and possibly outdated, information.

By providing models with access to specific data sources, grounding tethers their output to your data, which reduces the chances of the model inventing content (a behavior known as hallucination). This is particularly important in situations where accuracy and reliability are critical.

docs.title: Benefits of grounding
docs.text:
Grounding provides the following benefits:

  • Reduces model hallucinations, which are instances where the model generates content that isn't factual.
  • Anchors model responses to your specific data sources.
  • Enhances auditability by providing citations to the original sources.

docs.title: Grounding options in Vertex AI
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers several ways to ground model output. Use the following table to help you decide which option is best for your use case.

Grounding option Best for... Data source Grounding with Google Search Connecting your model to the vast, publicly available information on the internet. Google Search index Grounding with Google Maps Providing location-based, context-aware responses using Google Maps data. Google Maps Platform APIs Grounding Gemini with Elasticsearch Using your own private data stored in Elasticsearch to generate grounded responses (Retrieval-Augmented Generation). Your Elasticsearch indexes Web Grounding for Enterprise Grounding responses using a curated index of specific websites you define. A custom web index

docs.title: Web Grounding for Enterprise
docs.text: This page describes how to use the Web Grounding for Enterprise API to generate responses that are grounded on the web. The indexed content is a subset of what's available on Google Search and is suitable for customers in highly-regulated industries, such as finance, healthcare, and the public sector.

docs.title: When to use Web Grounding for Enterprise
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers two methods for grounding models on web content. Web Grounding for Enterprise is designed for organizations that require stringent compliance controls. If you don't require these controls, Grounding with Google Search offers access to a broader web index.

The following table provides a comparison between the two web grounding methods:

Feature Web Grounding for Enterprise Grounding with Google Search Compliance Designed for highly-regulated industries. Supports ML processing in US or EU multi-regions, no logging of customer data, and VPC Service Controls. General purpose; does not offer the same compliance controls. Data Handling No customer data is persisted. CMEK and Access Transparency are not applicable. Standard data handling policies apply. Web Index Uses a curated subset of the Google Search index suitable for enterprise use cases. Uses the comprehensive, full Google Search index. Ideal Use Case Generating grounded responses where data residency, no-logging, and other compliance features are critical. Applications that benefit from the broadest possible web knowledge and do not have strict compliance constraints.

docs.title: Use the API
docs.text:
To generate grounded responses with Web Grounding for Enterprise, you must provide the enterpriseWebSearch tool in your request to a Gemini model.

In your request, set the following fields:

  • Contents.parts.text: The text query you want to send to the API.
  • tools.enterpriseWebSearch: The tool that enables Web Grounding for Enterprise for Gemini.

The following examples show how to send a grounded request.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Python SDKREST

Install the SDK

To get started, install the Python SDK. 

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

Send a grounded request

Set environment variables to use the Gen AI SDK with Vertex AI, then run the following Python code.

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import (
    EnterpriseWebSearch,
    GenerateContentConfig,
    HttpOptions,
    Tool,
)

client = genai.Client(http_options=HttpOptions(api_version="v1"))

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="When is the next total solar eclipse in the United States?",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[
            # Use Enterprise Web Search Tool
            Tool(enterprise_web_search=EnterpriseWebSearch())
        ],
    ),
)

print(response.text)
# Example response:
# 'The next total solar eclipse in the United States will occur on ...'

Replace the following variables with your project's values:

  • PROJECT_NUMBER: Your project number.
  • LOCATION: Your region (for example, us-central1).
  • TEXT: Your prompt.
  curl -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "x-server-timeout: 60" \
    https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent -d '{
      "contents": [{
        "role": "user",
        "parts": [{
          "text": "TEXT"
        }]
      }],
      "tools": [{
        "enterpriseWebSearch": {}
      }]
    }'

docs.title: Base64 encode and decode files
docs.text: To include image or other binary data in a JSON REST request, you must encode that data as a Base64 string. This document shows you how to Base64 encode and decode files for use in Google Cloud API requests.

docs.title: Base64 encode files
docs.text:
When making a REST request, you must use JSON as the request body. JSON is a text format that doesn't support binary data directly, so you need to convert binary data into text using Base64 encoding.

Most development environments provide a native base64 utility to encode a binary file into ASCII text data. You can also use client libraries to handle encoding within your application workflow.

Method Best for Command line Quick, one-off tasks or simple shell scripting without a full application context. Client libraries Integrating encoding directly into your application's code for automated and repeatable workflows.

docs.title: Encode using the command line
docs.text:
To encode a file from the command line, use the utility that corresponds to your operating system.

LinuxmacOSWindowsPowerShell

Encode the file using the base64 command-line tool. Use the -w 0 flag to prevent line-wrapping.

base64 INPUT_FILE -w 0 > OUTPUT_FILE

Encode the file using the base64 command-line tool.

base64 -i INPUT_FILE -o OUTPUT_FILE

Encode the file using the Base64.exe tool.

Base64.exe -e INPUT_FILE > OUTPUT_FILE

Encode the file using the Convert.ToBase64String method.

[Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("./INPUT_FILE")) > OUTPUT_FILE

After encoding your file, you can inline the Base64-encoded data in your JSON request payload.

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT",
      "image": {
        "bytes_base64_encoded": "B64_BASE_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Encode using client libraries
docs.text:
Embedding binary data into requests manually is not practical for most applications. Instead, you can embed Base64-encoded files within your client code. All supported programming languages have built-in functions for Base64 encoding.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

PythonNode.jsJavaGo 
# Import the base64 encoding library.
import base64

# Pass the image data to an encoding function.
def encode_image(image):
    with open(image, "rb") as image_file:
        encoded_string = base64.b64encode(image_file.read())
    return encoded_string

// Read the file into memory.
var fs = require('fs');
var imageFile = fs.readFileSync('/path/to/file');

// Convert the image data to a Buffer and base64 encode it.
var encoded = Buffer.from(imageFile).toString('base64');

// Import the Base64 encoding library.
import org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64;

// Encode the image.
String encodedString = Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(imageFile.getBytes());

import (
    "bufio"
    "encoding/base64"
    "io"
    "os"
)

// Open image file.
f, _ := os.Open("image.jpg")

// Read entire image into byte slice.
reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
content, _ := io.ReadAll(reader)

// Encode image as base64.
base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(content)

docs.title: Base64 decode files
docs.text:
API responses return generated or edited images as Base64-encoded strings. You can use the following client library samples to decode this data and save it locally as an image file.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

PythonNode.jsJavaGo 
# Import the base64 encoding library.
import base64

# Pass the base64 encoded image data to a decoding function and save image file.
def decode_image(b64_encoded_string):
   with open("b64DecodedImage.png", "wb") as fh:
     fh.write(base64.decodebytes(b64_encoded_string))

var fs = require('fs');

// Create buffer object, specifying base64 as encoding
var buf = Buffer.from(base64str,'base64');

// Write buffer content to a file
fs.writeFile("b64DecodedImage.png", buf, function(error){
  if(error){
    throw error;
  }else{
    console.log('File created from base64 string');
    return true;
  }
});

// Import libraries
import org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64;
import org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils;

// Create new file
File file = new File("./b64DecodedImage.png");
// Convert base64 encoded string to byte array
byte[] bytes = Base64.decodeBase64("base64");
// Write out file
FileUtils.writeByteArrayToFile(file, bytes);

// Import packages
import (
   "encoding/base64"
   "io"
   "os"
)

// Add encoded file string
var b64 = `TWFuIGlz...Vhc3VyZS4=`

// Decode base64-encoded string
dec, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(b64)
if err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

// Create output file
f, err := os.Create("b64DecodedImage.png")
if err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
defer f.Close()

if _, err := f.Write(dec); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := f.Sync(); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

docs.title: Controlled Customization
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is in Preview.

To request access to use this Imagen feature, fill out the Imagen on Vertex AI access request form.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Controlled customization lets you influence the structure of a generated image by providing a guide image alongside your text prompt. This technique gives you fine-grained control over the output, ensuring the generated image adheres to the composition and shapes of the guide image while adopting the style described in your prompt.

Key parameters include: * Guide image type: The type of image used to control the generation. This can be a standard color image or a structural map like a Canny edge detection image. * Imagen Control scale: A value that determines how strongly the generated image should adhere to the guide image. A higher value means stricter adherence.

docs.title: Choosing a guide image type
docs.text:
You can guide the image generation process using different types of images. The primary methods involve using a standard RGB image or a pre-processed Canny edge map. The following table helps you decide which to use.

Guide Image Type Description Use Case Standard RGB The model automatically extracts structural cues (like edges and depth) from a standard color image to guide the generation. Best for when you want to quickly restyle an existing image without manual pre-processing. The model infers the structure for you. Canny Edge You provide a black-and-white image showing only the detected edges of a source image. Best for when you need precise control over the output's structure. By providing the edge map directly, you explicitly define the composition.

docs.text:

docs.title: Tune a custom subject model (standard and instant tuning)
docs.text:
Preview

This feature and documentation are available to approved users. To request access to use this Imagen feature, fill out the Imagen on Vertex AI access request form.

With Imagen, Google's text-to-image model, you can fine-tune a model to generate images of a specific person, object, or style. This process, known as subject tuning, allows you to create a personalized model that understands a new concept based on a small set of input images.

This document guides you through the two methods available for subject tuning: Standard tuning and Instant tuning.

docs.title: Before you begin: Choose a tuning method
docs.text:
Imagen on Vertex AI offers two methods for tuning a custom subject model. Choose the method that best fits your use case.

Feature Standard Tuning Instant Tuning Use Case High-quality, production-level models with greater style diversity. Quick previews, concept testing, and experimentation. Training Time Longer (e.g., 1-2 hours) Faster (e.g., 10-20 minutes) Input Images More images recommended (10-20) for best results. Fewer images required (4-8). Output Quality Higher fidelity and consistency. Good quality, suitable for rapid iteration.

docs.title: Model tuning workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the high-level workflow for tuning and using a custom subject model.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare your dataset] --> B[Tune the model]
    B --> C[Generate images with the tuned model]

    click A "#prepare-your-dataset"
    click B "#tune-the-model"
    click C "#generate-images-with-the-tuned-model"

docs.title: Prepare your dataset
docs.text:
To tune a model, you first need to gather a set of images that clearly depict your subject. The images should be high-quality and show the subject from various angles, in different lighting conditions, and against different backgrounds.

  • For Standard tuning: We recommend 10-20 images.
  • For Instant tuning: You can use as few as 4-8 images.

Upload your images to a Cloud Storage bucket.

docs.title: Tune the model
docs.text:
After preparing your dataset, you can start the tuning process using either the standard or instant method.

Standard tuningInstant tuning

The standard tuning method is ideal for creating high-quality models for production use.

Steps for standard tuning

1. Start the tuning job

You can start a tuning job using the Google Cloud console or the Vertex AI API. You will need to provide the following: * A name for your model. * The path to your dataset in Cloud Storage. * The base model to fine-tune (e.g., imagen-3.0). * A unique text identifier for your subject (e.g., a photo of sks person).

2. Monitor the job

Navigate to the Models section in the Vertex AI console to monitor the status of your tuning job. Standard tuning jobs typically take one to two hours to complete.

3. Access the tuned model

Once the job is complete, your new model will be available in your project's model registry.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with the tuning process, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

The instant tuning method is designed for rapid experimentation and concept validation.

Steps for instant tuning

1. Start the tuning job

The process for starting an instant tuning job is similar to standard tuning but is optimized for speed. You will provide: * A name for your model. * The path to your smaller dataset in Cloud Storage. * The base model and a unique text identifier.

2. Access the tuned model

Instant tuning jobs are much faster and are typically complete in 10 to 20 minutes. Once finished, the model is ready for use in your project.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with the tuning process, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Generate images with the tuned model
docs.text:
Once your model is tuned, you can use it to generate images by referencing the unique text identifier you assigned to your subject in your prompts.

For example, if your identifier is a photo of sks person, your prompt might be:

a photo of sks person smiling and wearing a blue hat

You can generate images using the Vertex AI Studio or the Vertex AI API.

docs.title: Tune a custom style model
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is in Preview.

This feature and its documentation are available to approved users. To request access to use this Imagen feature, fill out the Imagen on Vertex AI access request form.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Style tuning in Imagen on Vertex AI lets you create a custom model that generates images in a specific artistic style. By providing just a few example images (as few as 10) that represent your desired aesthetic, you can train a model to apply that style consistently to new images generated from different text prompts.

This is useful for maintaining a consistent brand identity, creating artwork with a unique signature look, or applying a specific photographic style across a series of images.

For example, you can train a model on images with a distinct "golden hour" photographic style and then use it to generate new images, like a freight truck, that adhere to that same visual theme.

docs.title: Style tuning example
docs.text:
The following example shows four images used to train a custom style model, and the resulting image generated by the tuned model from a new prompt.

Training images: Four images with a consistent "golden photo style" used to train a custom model. Generated image: An image created by the custom model from the prompt "A high quality photo of a freight truck in golden photo style."

docs.title: How to tune a style model
docs.text:
You can tune a style model using the Vertex AI API or the Google Cloud console. The following table can help you decide which option is best for your use case.

Method Best for Vertex AI API Automating your tuning and image generation workflows, integrating with existing applications, and programmatic control over all parameters. Google Cloud console Quickly experimenting with style tuning, visual feedback during the process, and managing models without writing code.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text:
This tutorial shows you how to tune a custom style model and use it to generate images.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare training data] --> B[Tune the model] --> C[Generate images with the tuned model]

    click A "#prepare-your-training-data"
    click B "#tune-the-model"
    click C "#generate-images-with-the-tuned-model"
Before you begin
  1. Set up your Google Cloud project: In the Google Cloud console, on the project selector page, select or create a Google Cloud project.
  2. Enable billing: Make sure that billing is enabled for your Google Cloud project.
  3. Enable the Vertex AI API: Enable the Vertex AI API.
  4. Set up authentication: How you set up authentication depends on the interface you use to access Vertex AI.
    • Google Cloud console: You don't need to set up authentication to use the console.
    • Vertex AI API: If you are using a client library or the Vertex AI SDK for Python, you can set up Application Default Credentials (ADC). For more information, see Set up authentication for Vertex AI.
Step 1: Prepare your training data

To tune a style model, you need a small dataset of 10 to 20 images that clearly represent the style you want to replicate.

Vertex AI APIGoogle Cloud console
  1. Collect your images: Gather 10-20 high-quality images in your desired style.
  2. Upload to Cloud Storage: Create a Cloud Storage bucket and upload your images to it. 
    gsutil mb gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME
gsutil -m cp /local/path/to/images/*.jpg gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-images/
  3. Create a JSONL file: Create a JSON Lines file that points to your images in the Cloud Storage bucket. Each line should contain a file_path key. 
    {"file_path": "gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-images/image1.jpg"}
{"file_path": "gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-images/image2.jpg"}
...
  4. Upload the JSONL file to your Cloud Storage bucket.
  1. Collect your images: Gather 10-20 high-quality images in your desired style on your local machine.
  2. Navigate to Imagen: In the Google Cloud console, go to the Imagen section.
  3. Start a tuning job: In the Tune & filter tab, click Tune a model and select Style tuning. The console UI will guide you to upload your images directly from your computer.
Step 2: Tune the model

After preparing your data, you can start the tuning job.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Vertex AI APIGoogle Cloud console

Use the TuningJob resource to start a style tuning job. You will need to specify the base model, the path to your training data JSONL file, and a name for your tuned model.

# Example using the Vertex AI SDK for Python
from google.cloud import aiplatform

aiplatform.init(project="YOUR_PROJECT_ID", location="us-central1")

tuning_job = aiplatform.ModelGarden.get_tuned_model(
    source_model_id="imagen-3.0-fast-style-tuner",
    display_name="my-golden-photo-style-model",
    training_data_uri="gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME/style-training-data.jsonl",
    train_steps=1000,
)

print(f"Tuning job created: {tuning_job.resource_name}")
  1. In the style tuning workflow you started in the previous step, give your model a name.
  2. Select the base model you want to tune.
  3. Click Start Tuning. You can monitor the progress of the job in the console.
Step 3: Generate images with the tuned model

Once the tuning job is complete, your custom model is ready to use.

Vertex AI APIGoogle Cloud console

You can get predictions from your tuned model by referencing its resource name or ID.

# Example using the Vertex AI SDK for Python
from vertexai.preview.vision_models import ImageGenerationModel

# Use the resource name from the tuning job output
tuned_model = ImageGenerationModel.from_pretrained("projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/models/YOUR_MODEL_ID")

response = tuned_model.generate_images(
    prompt="A high quality photo of a freight truck in golden photo style.",
    number_of_images=1,
)

response.images[0].save(location="generated_truck.png", include_generation_parameters=True)
  1. Once your model is finished tuning, it will appear in the Tune & filter tab.
  2. Select your model and click Generate Images.
  3. Enter a prompt, such as "A high quality photo of a freight truck in golden photo style," and click Generate.

docs.title: Generate images with text
docs.text:
To see examples of image generation using Imagen, run the following Jupyter notebooks in the environment of your choice:

  • Image Generation with Imagen on Vertex AI:

    Open in Colab | Open in Colab Enterprise | Open in Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebooks | View on GitHub

  • Create High Quality Visual Assets with Imagen and Gemini:

    Open in Colab | Open in Colab Enterprise | Open in Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebooks | View on GitHub

You can generate novel images using only descriptive text as an input. The following samples show you basic instructions to generate images, but you can also use additional parameters depending on your use case.

ConsolePythonREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. Click Image.

  3. Optional: In the Settings pane, configure the following settings:
    • Model: Choose a model from the available options. For more information, see Imagen models.
    • Aspect ratio: Choose an aspect ratio from the available options.
    • Number of results: Adjust the slider or enter a value between 1 and 4.
    • Negative prompt: Enter a prompt that describes what you don't want generated in the image (supported models only).
  4. Optional: In the Advanced options section, select a Region to generate your images in.
  5. Optional: In the Safety section, configure Person generation and Safety filter threshold settings.
  6. Optional: In the Style section, choose a predefined style from the menu (supported models only).
  7. In the Write your prompt box, enter your text prompt that describes the images to generate. For example, small boat on water in the morning watercolor illustration.
    • To get help writing your prompt, click Help me write to use the prompt enhancement feature.
  8. Click Generate.

A digital watermark is automatically added to generated images. You can't disable the digital watermark for image generation using the Google Cloud console. You can select an image to view it in the Image detail window.

Image detail view of a watermarked image generated with Imagen 2 from the prompt: small red boat on water in the morning watercolor illustration muted colors.

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Before you begin section. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

In this sample, you call the generate_images method on the ImageGenerationModel and save generated images locally. You can then optionally use the show() method in a notebook to show you the generated images. For more information on model versions and features, see Imagen models.

from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below line
# output_file = "output-image.png"

image = client.models.generate_images(
    model="imagen-4.0-generate-preview-06-06",
    prompt="A dog reading a newspaper",
)

image.generated_images[0].image.save(output_file)

print(f"Created output image using {len(image.generated_images[0].image.image_bytes)} bytes")
# Example response:
# Created output image using 1234567 bytes

For more information about imagegeneration model requests, see the imagegeneration model API reference.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict

Request body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "TEXT_PROMPT"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": 4
  }
}

Request parameters:

The following table provides a summary of the parameters for an image generation request.

Field Type Description prompt string Required. The text prompt that guides what images the model generates. sampleCount integer The number of images to generate. Default: 4. Max: 8 (model dependent). addWatermark boolean Whether to add a digital watermark. Default: true. aspectRatio string The aspect ratio of the generated image (e.g., 1:1, 16:9). enhancePrompt boolean Enables an LLM-based prompt rewriter for higher quality images. Default: true. language string The language of the input text prompt (e.g., en, es, ja). negativePrompt string A description of what to omit in the generated images. seed integer A number to make generated images deterministic. Requires addWatermark to be false. personGeneration string Safety setting to control generation of people (e.g., allow_adult, dont_allow). safetySetting string Controls safety filter thresholds (e.g., block_medium_and_above). includeRaiReason boolean Whether to include the reason for a Responsible AI filter block. Default: false. includeSafetyAttributes boolean Whether to include Responsible AI safety scores. Default: false. sampleImageStyle string A predefined style for the image (e.g., photograph, watercolor). storageUri string A Cloud Storage bucket to store output images. outputOptions object Options for the output file, such as mimeType and compressionQuality. View parameter details

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • MODEL_VERSION: The imagegeneration model version to use. For a list of available models, see Imagen models.
  • TEXT_PROMPT: The text prompt that guides what images the model generates.

Request Parameters:

  • sampleCount: integer. The number of generated images. Accepted integer values: 1-8 (imagegeneration@002), 1-4 (all other model versions). Default value: 4.
  • addWatermark: boolean. Optional. Whether to enable a watermark for generated images. Any image generated when the field is set to true contains a digital SynthID that you can use to verify a watermarked image. If you omit this field, the default value of true is used; you must set the value to false to disable this feature. You can use the seed field to get deterministic output only when this field is set to false.
  • aspectRatio: string. Optional. A generation mode parameter that controls aspect ratio. Supported ratio values and their intended use: 1:1 (default, square), 3:4 (Ads, social media), 4:3 (TV, photography), 16:9 (landscape), 9:16 (portrait).
  • enhancePrompt: boolean. Optional. A parameter to use an LLM-based prompt rewriting feature to deliver higher quality images that better reflect the original prompt's intent. Disabling this feature may impact image quality and prompt adherence. Default value: true.
  • includeRaiReason: boolean. Optional. Whether to enable the Responsible AI filtered reason code in responses with blocked input or output. Default value: false.
  • includeSafetyAttributes: boolean. Optional. Whether to enable rounded Responsible AI scores for a list of safety attributes in responses for unfiltered input and output. Safety attribute categories: "Death, Harm & Tragedy", "Firearms & Weapons", "Hate", "Health", "Illicit Drugs", "Politics", "Porn", "Religion & Belief", "Toxic", "Violence", "Vulgarity", "War & Conflict". Default value: false.
  • outputOptions: object. Optional. Contains the following fields:
    • mimeType: string. The MIME type of the content of the image. Available values: image/jpeg, image/gif, image/png, image/webp, image/bmp, image/tiff, image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
    • compressionQuality: integer. Only applies to JPEG output files. The level of detail the model preserves for images generated in JPEG file format. Values: 0 to 100, where a higher number means more compression. Default: 75.
  • personGeneration: string. Optional. The safety setting that controls the type of people or face generation the model allows. Available values: allow_adult (default), dont_allow.
  • safetySetting: string. Optional. A setting that controls safety filter thresholds for generated images. Available values: block_low_and_above, block_medium_and_above (default), block_only_high.
  • seed: integer. Optional. Any non-negative integer you provide to make output images deterministic. Providing the same seed number always results in the same output images. If the model you're using supports digital watermarking, you must set "addWatermark": false to use this field. Accepted integer values: 1 - 2147483647.
  • storageUri: string. Optional. The Cloud Storage bucket to store the output images. If not provided, base64-encoded image bytes are returned in the response. Sample value: gs://image-bucket/output/.
  • negativePrompt: string. Optional. A description of what you want to omit in generated images. For example, "people".
  • language: string. Optional. The language code that corresponds to your text prompt language. Available values: auto, en (default), es, hi, ja, ko, pt, zh-TW, zh or zh-CN.
  • sampleImageStyle: string. Optional. A predefined style for the image. Available values: photograph, digital_art, landscape, sketch, watercolor, cyberpunk, pop_art.

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/MODEL_VERSION:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Sample response:

The following sample response is for a request with "sampleCount": 2. The response returns two prediction objects, with the generated image bytes base64-encoded.

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES"
    }
  ]
}

If you use a model that supports prompt enhancement, the response includes an additional prompt field with the enhanced prompt used for generation:

{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
      "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_1",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_1"
    },
    {
      "mimeType": "MIME_TYPE",
      "prompt": "ENHANCED_PROMPT_2",
      "bytesBase64Encoded": "BASE64_IMG_BYTES_2"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Upscale an image
docs.text:
Use upscaling to increase the size of existing, generated, or edited images without losing quality.

ConsoleREST

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Vertex AI Studio > Media Studio page.

    Go to Media Studio

  2. Click Image.

  3. In the Write your prompt box, enter your text prompt that describes the images to generate.
  4. Click Generate.
  5. Click an image to upscale. The Image pane is displayed.
  6. Click Export image. The Export image dialog is displayed.
  7. Click Also upscale image and then select a Scale factor.
  8. To download the upscaled image, click Export.

When you upscale an image using the API, specify "mode": "upscale" and upscaleConfig in the parameters object.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • B64_BASE_IMAGE: The base image to upscale, specified as a base64-encoded byte string. Size limit: 10 MB.
  • IMAGE_SOURCE: The Cloud Storage location of the image you want to upscale. For example: gs://output-bucket/source-photos/photo.png.
  • UPSCALE_FACTOR: Optional. The factor to which the image will be upscaled. Available values: x2 or x4.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict

Request JSON body:

In the image object, use either bytesBase64Encoded or gcsUri to specify the image to upscale.

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "prompt": "",
      "image": {
        "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_BASE_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": 1,
    "mode": "upscale",
    "upscaleConfig": {
      "upscaleFactor": "UPSCALE_FACTOR"
    }
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login , or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI . You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagegeneration@002:predict"

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token

docs.title: Responsible AI safety filtering
docs.text:
The image captioning and Visual Question Answering (VQA) feature model doesn't support user-configurable safety filters. However, the overall Imagen safety filtering occurs on the following data:

  • User input
  • Model output

As a result, your output may differ from the sample output if Imagen applies these safety filters. Consider the following examples.

docs.title: Filtered input
docs.text:
If the input is filtered, the response is similar to the following:

{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "details": [
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.DebugInfo",
        "detail": "[ORIGINAL ERROR] generic::invalid_argument: Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394 [google.rpc.error_details_ext] { message: \"Media reasoning failed with the following error: The response is blocked, as it may violate our policies. If you believe this is an error, please send feedback to your account team. Error Code: 63429089, 72817394\" }"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Filtered output
docs.text:
If the number of responses returned is less than the sample count you specify, this means the missing responses are filtered by Responsible AI. For example, the following is a response to a request with "sampleCount": 2, but one of the responses is filtered out:

{
  "predictions": [
    "cappuccino"
  ]
}

If all the output is filtered, the response is an empty object similar to the following:

{}

docs.title: Get short-form image captions
docs.text:
Use the following samples to generate short-form captions for an image.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPythonNode.js

For more information about imagetext model requests, see the imagetext model API reference.

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • PROJECT_ID: Your Google Cloud project ID.
  • LOCATION: Your project's region. For example, us-central1, europe-west2, or asia-northeast3. For a list of available regions, see Generative AI on Vertex AI locations.
  • B64_IMAGE: The image to get captions for. The image must be specified as a base64-encoded byte string. Size limit: 10 MB.
  • RESPONSE_COUNT: The number of image captions you want to generate. Accepted integer values: 1-3.
  • LANGUAGE_CODE: One of the supported language codes.

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict

Request JSON body:

{
  "instances": [
    {
      "image": {
          "bytesBase64Encoded": "B64_IMAGE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "sampleCount": RESPONSE_COUNT,
    "language": "LANGUAGE_CODE"
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of these options. The following commands assume that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell.

curlPowerShell

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     -d @request.json \
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict"

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }

Invoke-WebRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Headers $headers `
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `
    -InFile request.json `
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/google/models/imagetext:predict" | Select-Object -Expand Content

The following sample responses are for a request with "sampleCount": 2.

English (en):

{
  "predictions": [
    "a yellow mug with a sheep on it sits next to a slice of cake",
    "a cup of coffee with a heart shaped latte art next to a slice of cake"
  ],
  "deployedModelId": "DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID",
  "model": "projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/models/MODEL_ID",
  "modelDisplayName": "MODEL_DISPLAYNAME",
  "modelVersionId": "1"
}

Spanish (es):

{
  "predictions": [
    "una taza de café junto a un plato de pastel de chocolate",
    "una taza de café con una forma de corazón en la espuma"
  ]
}

Before trying this sample, follow the Python setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Python API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

In this sample you use the load_from_file method to reference a local file as the base Image to get a caption for. After you specify the base image, you use the get_captions method on the ImageTextModel and print the output.

import vertexai
from vertexai.preview.vision_models import Image, ImageTextModel

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# input_file = "input-image.png"

vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

model = ImageTextModel.from_pretrained("imagetext@001")
source_img = Image.load_from_file(location=input_file)

captions = model.get_captions(
    image=source_img,
    # Optional parameters
    language="en",
    number_of_results=2,
)

print(captions)
# Example response:
# ['a cat with green eyes looks up at the sky']

Before trying this sample, follow the Node.js setup instructions in the Vertex AI quickstart using client libraries. For more information, see the Vertex AI Node.js API reference documentation.

To authenticate to Vertex AI, set up Application Default Credentials. For more information, see Set up authentication for a local development environment.

In this sample, you call the predict method on a PredictionServiceClient. The service returns captions for the provided image.

/**
 * TODO(developer): Update these variables before running the sample.
 */
const projectId = process.env.CAIP_PROJECT_ID;
const location = 'us-central1';
const inputFile = 'resources/cat.png';

const aiplatform = require('@google-cloud/aiplatform');

// Imports the Google Cloud Prediction Service Client library
const {PredictionServiceClient} = aiplatform.v1;

// Import the helper module for converting arbitrary protobuf.Value objects
const {helpers} = aiplatform;

// Specifies the location of the api endpoint
const clientOptions = {
  apiEndpoint: `${location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`,
};

// Instantiates a client
const predictionServiceClient = new PredictionServiceClient(clientOptions);

async function getShortFormImageCaptions() {
  const fs = require('fs');
  // Configure the parent resource
  const endpoint = `projects/${projectId}/locations/${location}/publishers/google/models/imagetext@001`;

  const imageFile = fs.readFileSync(inputFile);
  // Convert the image data to a Buffer and base64 encode it.
  const encodedImage = Buffer.from(imageFile).toString('base64');

  const instance = {
    image: {
      bytesBase64Encoded: encodedImage,
    },
  };
  const instanceValue = helpers.toValue(instance);
  const instances = [instanceValue];

  const parameter = {
    // Optional parameters
    language: 'en',
    sampleCount: 2,
  };
  const parameters = helpers.toValue(parameter);

  const request = {
    endpoint,
    instances,
    parameters,
  };

  // Predict request
  const [response] = await predictionServiceClient.predict(request);
  const predictions = response.predictions;
  if (predictions.length === 0) {
    console.log(
      'No captions were generated. Check the request parameters and image.'
    );
  } else {
    predictions.forEach(prediction => {
      console.log(prediction.stringValue);
    });
  }
}
await getShortFormImageCaptions();

docs.title: Use parameters for image captioning
docs.text:
When you get image captions there are several parameters you can set depending on your use case.

Number of results

Use the number of results parameter to limit the amount of captions returned for each request you send. For more information, see the imagetext (image captioning) model API reference.

Seed number

A number you add to a request to make generated descriptions deterministic. Adding a seed number with your request is a way to assure you get the same prediction (descriptions) each time. However, the image captions aren't necessarily returned in the same order. For more information, see the imagetext (image captioning) model API reference.
