Anthropic recommends that you enable 30-day logging of your prompt and completion activity to record any model misuse. To enable logging, see Log requests and responses.

docs.title: Send prediction requests
docs.text:
After you complete the setup, you can send requests to the Claude models. You can use the Anthropic SDK for a higher-level programmatic interface or cURL for direct REST API calls.

Method Best for Pros Cons Anthropic SDK Application development and integration. - Simplified API calls.- Handles authentication and request formatting automatically.- Available for Python and TypeScript. - Requires installing and managing a client library.- Adds a dependency to your project. cURL Quick testing, scripting, and environments where installing an SDK is not feasible. - No installation required (pre-installed on most systems).- Direct control over the HTTP request. - Requires manual construction of JSON payloads.- Authentication token management is manual.- Can be more verbose and error-prone.

Select a tab for instructions on how to use each method.

Anthropic SDKcURL

You can make API requests to the Claude models using the Anthropic Claude SDK. For more information, see the following resources: * Claude messages API reference * Anthropic Python API library * Anthropic Vertex AI TypeScript API Library

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Vertex AI SDK for Python API reference documentation.

docs.title: Build the request
docs.text:
HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/anthropic/models/MODEL:streamRawPredict
View parameter descriptions

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: A region that supports Anthropic Claude models. To use the global endpoint, see Specify the global endpoint.
  • MODEL: The model name you want to use.
  • ROLE: The role associated with a message. You can specify a user or an assistant. The first message must use the user role. Claude models operate with alternating user and assistant turns. If the final message uses the assistant role, then the response content continues immediately from the content in that message. You can use this to constrain part of the model's response.
  • STREAM: A boolean that specifies whether the response is streamed or not. Stream your response to reduce the end-use latency perception. Set to true to stream the response and false to return the response all at once.
  • CONTENT: The content, such as text, of the user or assistant message.
  • MAX_TOKENS: Maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the response. A token is approximately 3.5 characters. 100 tokens correspond to roughly 60-80 words. Specify a lower value for shorter responses and a higher value for potentially longer responses.
  • TOP_P (Optional): Top-P changes how the model selects tokens for output. Tokens are selected from the most probable to least probable until the sum of their probabilities equals the top-P value. For example, if tokens A, B, and C have a probability of 0.3, 0.2, and 0.1 and the top-P value is 0.5, then the model will select either A or B as the next token by using temperature and excludes C as a candidate. Specify a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.
  • TOP_K (Optional): Top-K changes how the model selects tokens for output. A top-K of 1 means the next selected token is the most probable among all tokens in the model's vocabulary (also called greedy decoding), while a top-K of 3 means that the next token is selected from among the three most probable tokens by using temperature. For each token selection step, the top-K tokens with the highest probabilities are sampled. Then tokens are further filtered based on top-P with the final token selected using temperature sampling. Specify a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.
  • TYPE: For Claude 3.7 Sonnet and later Claude models, to enable extended thinking mode, specify enable.
  • BUDGET_TOKENS: If you enable extended thinking, you must specify the number of tokens that the model can use for its internal reasoning as part of the output. Larger budgets can enable more thorough analysis for complex problems and improve response quality. You must specify a value greater than or equal to 1024 but less than MAX_TOKENS.

Request JSON body:

{
  "anthropic_version": "vertex-2023-10-16",
  "messages": [
   {
    "role": "ROLE",
    "content": "CONTENT"
   }],
  "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS,
  "stream": STREAM,
  "thinking": {
    "type": "TYPE",
    "budget_tokens": BUDGET_TOKENS
  }
}

docs.text:
The Anthropic Claude models support tools and function calling to enhance a model's capabilities. For more information, see the Tool use overview in the Anthropic documentation.

The following samples demonstrate how to use tools to search for nearby restaurants in San Francisco that are open.

Vertex AI SDK for PythonREST

The following sample uses regional endpoints. To use the global endpoint, see Specify the global endpoint.

docs.title: Use Vertex AI Studio
docs.text:
For some of the Anthropic Claude models, you can use Vertex AI Studio to quickly prototype and test generative AI models in the Google Cloud console. As an example, you can use Vertex AI Studio to compare Claude model responses with other supported models such as Google Gemini.

For more information, see Quickstart: Send text prompts to Gemini using Vertex AI Studio.

docs.title: Anthropic Claude quotas and region availability
docs.text:
Claude models have regional quotas and, for models that support a global endpoint, a global quota. The quota is specified in queries per minute (QPM) and tokens per minute (TPM). TPM includes both input and output tokens.

To maintain overall service performance and acceptable use, the maximum quotas might vary by account and, in some cases, access might be restricted. View your project's quotas on the Quotas & Systems Limits page in the Google Cloud console. You must also have the following quotas available:

  • online_prediction_requests_per_base_model and global_online_prediction_requests_per_base_model defines your QPM quota.
  • For TPM, there are three quota values that apply to particular models:
    • For models that count input and output tokens together, online_prediction_tokens_per_minute_per_base_model and global_online_prediction_tokens_per_minute_per_base_model defines the model TPM quota.
    • For models that count input and output tokens separately, online_prediction_input_tokens_per_minute_per_base_model and global_online_prediction_input_tokens_per_minute_per_base_model defines the input TPM quota and online_prediction_output_tokens_per_minute_per_base_model and global_online_prediction_output_tokens_per_minute_per_base_model defines the output TPM quota.

To see which models count input and output tokens separately, see Quotas by model and region.

docs.title: Input tokens
docs.text:
The following list defines the input tokens that can count towards your input TPM quota. The input tokens that each model counts can vary. To see which input tokens a model counts, see Quotas by model and region.

  • Input tokens includes all input tokens, including cache read and cache write tokens.
  • Uncached input tokens includes only the input tokens that weren't read from a cache (cache read tokens).
  • Cache write tokens includes tokens that were used to create or update a cache.

docs.title: Batch predictions
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Batch predictions let you efficiently send a large number of text-only prompts to a Llama model in a single request. This method is ideal for non-latency-sensitive tasks, as it offers a cost-effective way to process prompts in bulk compared to online predictions.

There are no charges for batch predictions during the Preview period.

docs.title: Supported Llama models
docs.text:
Vertex AI supports batch predictions for the following Llama models:

  • Llama 3.1 405B
  • Llama 3.1 70B
  • Llama 3.1 8B

docs.title: Batch prediction workflow
docs.text:
The process for getting batch predictions involves preparing your input data, submitting a batch prediction job, checking the job's status, and retrieving the output.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare input data] --> B[Request a batch prediction job]
    B --> C[Get the job status]
    C --> D[Retrieve prediction output]

    click A "#prepare-your-input-data"
    click B "#request-a-batch-prediction-job"
    click C "#get-the-job-status"
    click D "#retrieve-prediction-output"

docs.title: Prepare your input data
docs.text:
You can provide your input prompts from either a BigQuery table or a JSON Lines (JSONL) file in a Cloud Storage bucket.

Input Source Description BigQuery Use a BigQuery table for your input. This is useful if your data already resides in BigQuery. Cloud Storage Use a JSONL file stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. This is a flexible option for file-based workflows.

Regardless of the source, each input prompt must follow the OpenAI API chat completions schema in JSON format.

View an example input record

The following shows a single record in the required JSON format. For a JSONL file, each line would be a JSON object like this. For a BigQuery table, this JSON object would be the value in the body column.

{"custom_id": "test-request-0", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "meta/llama-3.1-405b-instruct-maas", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a chef."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Give me a recipe for banana bread"}], "max_tokens": 1000}}
Note: Vertex AI doesn't use the custom_id, method, url, and model fields. You can include them, but they are ignored by the batch prediction job.

Input source requirements

BigQuery

Your BigQuery input table must contain a column named body of type JSON. This column holds the prompt data.

  • Your input table can have other columns. These are ignored by the batch job but are passed through to the output table, which can be useful for joining results with your original data.
  • Batch prediction jobs reserve two column names for the output: response(JSON) and id. Do not use these column names in your input table.

Cloud Storage

For Cloud Storage, the input file must be a JSONL file where each line is a valid JSON object representing a single prediction request. The file must be located in a Cloud Storage bucket.

docs.title: Request a batch prediction job
docs.text:
After preparing your input data, you can request a batch prediction job using the REST API. You can choose to receive the output in either a BigQuery table or a Cloud Storage bucket, regardless of your input source.

Before you begin

Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: A region that supports Llama models.
  • PROJECT_ID: Your project ID.
  • JOB_NAME: A display name for your batch prediction job (e.g., llama_batch_job_1).
  • MODEL: The name of the model to use. For example, llama-3.1-405b-instruct-maas.
  • INPUT_URI: The URI of your input data.
    • For BigQuery: bq://PROJECT_ID.DATASET_ID.TABLE_ID
    • For Cloud Storage: gs://BUCKET_NAME/PATH/TO/YOUR_FILE.jsonl
  • OUTPUT_FORMAT: The format for the prediction output. Specify bigquery for a BigQuery table or jsonl for a JSONL file in Cloud Storage.
  • DESTINATION: The field name for the output configuration. Specify bigqueryDestination for BigQuery or gcsDestination for Cloud Storage.
  • OUTPUT_URI_FIELD_NAME: The field name for the output URI. Specify outputUri for BigQuery or outputUriPrefix for Cloud Storage.
  • OUTPUT_URI: The destination path for your output.
    • For BigQuery: bq://PROJECT_ID.DATASET_ID.TABLE_ID
    • For Cloud Storage: gs://BUCKET_NAME/PATH/TO/OUTPUT/

HTTP method and URL:

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/batchPredictionJobs
From BigQueryFrom Cloud Storage

Request JSON body:

{
  "displayName": "JOB_NAME",
  "model": "publishers/meta/models/MODEL",
  "inputConfig": {
    "instancesFormat":"bigquery",
    "bigquerySource":{
      "inputUri" : "INPUT_URI"
    }
  },
  "outputConfig": {
    "predictionsFormat":"OUTPUT_FORMAT",
    "DESTINATION":{
      "OUTPUT_URI_FIELD_NAME": "OUTPUT_URI"
    }
  }
}

Request JSON body:

{
  "displayName": "JOB_NAME",
  "model": "publishers/meta/models/MODEL",
  "inputConfig": {
    "instancesFormat":"jsonl",
    "gcsSource":{
      "uris" : ["INPUT_URI"]
    }
  },
  "outputConfig": {
    "predictionsFormat":"OUTPUT_FORMAT",
    "DESTINATION":{
      "OUTPUT_URI_FIELD_NAME": "OUTPUT_URI"
    }
  }
}

To send your request, save the request body in a file named request.json and choose one of the following options:

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

curl

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Execute the following command:

     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \

docs.title: Retrieve prediction output
docs.text:
Once your batch prediction job has succeeded, the results are available in the output location you specified.

  • For BigQuery output: The predictions are in a new column named response (JSON type) in your destination BigQuery table.
  • For Cloud Storage output: The predictions are saved as one or more JSONL files in the specified output bucket and folder.
View a sample output record

Each output record contains the model's response to a corresponding input prompt. The following is an example of a single line from an output JSONL file or the content of the response column in a BigQuery table.

docs.title: Send chat requests to a Llama model
docs.text:
You can send requests to a Llama model as a streaming call or a unary call.

Call Type Description Use Case Streaming The model sends the response in chunks as they are generated. Best for interactive applications where users are waiting for a response, as it reduces perceived latency. Unary The model sends the entire response at once after it has been fully generated. Suitable for offline or batch processing tasks where the complete response is needed before further processing can occur.

docs.title: Request parameters
docs.text:
Before using any of the request data, make the following replacements:

  • LOCATION: A region that supports Llama models. For details, see Llama model region availability and quotas.
  • MODEL: The model name you want to use. For details, see Available Llama models.
  • ROLE: The role associated with a message. You can specify a user or an assistant. The first message must use the user role. The models operate with alternating user and assistant turns.
  • CONTENT: The text content of the user or assistant message.
  • MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS: The maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the response. A token is approximately four characters. 100 tokens correspond to roughly 60-80 words.
  • ENABLE_LLAMA_GUARD: A boolean that specifies whether to enable Llama Guard on your inputs and outputs. By default, Llama Guard is enabled and flags responses if it determines they are unsafe.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Streaming callUnary call

A streaming call sends the response back in chunks as it's generated.

HTTP method and URL

POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints/openapi/chat/completions

Request JSON body

{
  "model": "meta/MODEL",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "ROLE",
      "content": "CONTENT"
    }
  ],
  "max_tokens": MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
  "stream": true,
  "extra_body": {
    "google": {
      "model_safety_settings": {
        "enabled": ENABLE_LLAMA_GUARD,
        "llama_guard_settings": {}
      }
    }
  }
}

To send your request, choose one of the following options:

curlPowerShell

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login, or by using Cloud Shell, which automatically logs you into the gcloud CLI. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

curl -X POST \  
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \  
     -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \  
     -d @request.json \  
     "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints/openapi/chat/completions"

Note: The following command assumes that you have logged in to the gcloud CLI with your user account by running gcloud init or gcloud auth login. You can check the currently active account by running gcloud auth list.

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

$cred = gcloud auth print-access-token  
$headers = @{ "Authorization" = "Bearer $cred" }  

Invoke-WebRequest `  
    -Method POST `  
    -Headers $headers `  
    -ContentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8" `  
    -InFile request.json `  
    -Uri "https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/endpoints/openapi/chat/completions" | Select-Object -Expand Content

Response

You should receive a JSON response similar to the following. The response is sent in chunks. If Llama Guard is used and the response is flagged, the refusal field will contain the reason.

data: {
  "choices": [
    {
      "delta": {
        "content": "CONTENT",
        "role": "assistant",
        "refusal": "REFUSAL_REASON"
      },
      "index": 0
    }
  ],
  "model": "meta/MODEL_NAME",
  "object": "chat.completion.chunk"
}

data: {
  "choices": [
    {
      "delta": {
        "content": "CONTENT",
        "role": "assistant"
      },
      "finish_reason": "stop",
      "index": 0
    }
  ],
  "model": "meta/MODEL_NAME",
  "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
  "usage": {
    "completion_tokens": 131,
    "prompt_tokens": 14,
    "total_tokens": 145
  }
}

A unary call sends the entire response at once after it has been fully generated.

HTTP method and URL

Request JSON body

Save the request body in a file named request.json, and execute the following command:

docs.title: Flagged responses
docs.text:
By default, Llama Guard is enabled on all predictions that you make with Llama models. * Llama Guard 3 8B is used for Llama 3.3 and Llama 3.1 models. * Llama Guard 3 11B vision is used for Llama 3.2 models.

Llama Guard helps safeguard responses by checking inputs and outputs. If Llama Guard determines they are unsafe, it flags the response.

If you want to disable Llama Guard, set the enabled field to false in the model_safety_settings of your request.

docs.title: Use this model
docs.text:
The following Python example shows how to use the mistral-small-2503 model to generate text.

import vertexai
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel

def generate_text(project_id: str, location: str) -> str:
    """Generates text using the Mistral Small model."""
    # Initialize Vertex AI
    vertexai.init(project=project_id, location=location)

    # Load the model
    model = GenerativeModel(model_name="mistral-small-2503")

    # Generate content
    response = model.generate_content("Why is the sky blue?")

    return response.text

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Error code 429
docs.text:
When the number of requests sent to a model exceeds the available processing capacity, Vertex AI returns a 429 error code, which indicates a resource quota has been exhausted. The specific error message and cause depend on whether you are using a pay-as-you-go plan or have purchased Provisioned Throughput.

The following table explains the 429 error for each quota framework.

Quota framework Error Message Cause Pay-as-you-go Resource exhausted, please try again later. Your requests have exceeded the available on-demand capacity. This can be due to traffic spikes or exceeding regional quotas. Provisioned Throughput Too many requests. Exceeded the Provisioned Throughput. Your request rate has surpassed the throughput amount you reserved with your subscription.

With a Provisioned Throughput subscription, you reserve a specific amount of throughput for your models. If you don't have a subscription and on-demand resources aren't available, you receive a 429 error. While you can retry the request, it isn't counted against your error rate as described in the service level agreement (SLA).

For projects with Provisioned Throughput, Vertex AI reserves the purchased throughput for your usage. * If you use less than your purchased throughput, errors that might otherwise be 429 are returned as 5XX and are counted as part of the error rate described in the SLA. * If you use more than your purchased throughput, the additional requests are processed on-demand as pay-as-you-go, unless you configure them to fail.

docs.title: Resolve 429 errors
docs.text:
To resolve 429 errors, choose the tab that corresponds to your quota framework.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter other issues with your setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Pay-as-you-goProvisioned Throughput

On the pay-as-you-go quota framework, you have the following options to resolve 429 errors:

  • Use the global endpoint: Use the global endpoint instead of a regional endpoint whenever possible.
  • Implement a retry strategy: Use truncated exponential backoff to manage request retries.
  • Manage quotas:
    • If your model uses standard quotas, you can submit a Quota Increase Request (QIR).
    • If your model uses Dynamic Shared Quota, smoothing traffic and reducing large spikes can help. For more information, see Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ).
  • Subscribe to Provisioned Throughput: For a more consistent level of service, purchase a Provisioned Throughput subscription. For more information, see Provisioned Throughput.

To resolve 429 errors when using Provisioned Throughput, you have the following options:

  • Allow on-demand overages: Use the default behavior, which doesn't set a header in prediction requests. Any requests that exceed your provisioned capacity are processed on-demand and billed as pay-as-you-go.
  • Increase your subscription: Increase the number of GSUs in your Provisioned Throughput subscription to handle a higher volume of requests.

docs.title: Calculate Provisioned Throughput requirements
docs.text: This section explains the concepts of generative AI scale unit (GSU) and burndown rates. Provisioned Throughput is calculated and priced using GSUs and burndown rates.

docs.title: GSU and burndown rate
docs.text:
A generative AI scale unit (GSU) is a measure of throughput for your prompts and responses. This amount specifies how much throughput to provision a model with.

A burndown rate is a ratio that converts the input and output units (such as tokens, characters, or images) to a standard unit (for example, input tokens per second). This ratio represents the throughput and is used to produce a standard unit across models.

Different models use different amounts of throughput. For information about the minimum GSU purchase amount and increments for each model, see Supported models and burndown rates.

This equation demonstrates how throughput is calculated:

inputs_per_query = inputs_across_modalities_converted_using_burndown_rates
outputs_per_query = outputs_across_modalities_converted_using_burndown_rates

throughput_per_second = (inputs_per_query + outputs_per_query) * queries_per_second

The calculated throughput per second determines how many GSUs you need for your use case.

docs.title: Important Considerations
docs.text:
To help you plan for your Provisioned Throughput needs, review the following important considerations:

  • Requests are prioritized. Provisioned Throughput customers are prioritized and serviced first before on-demand requests.
  • Throughput doesn't accumulate. Unused throughput doesn't accumulate or carry over to the next month.
  • Provisioned Throughput is measured in tokens per second, characters per second, or images per second. Provisioned Throughput isn't measured solely based on queries per minute (QPM). It's measured based on the query size for your use case, the response size, and the QPM.
  • Provisioned Throughput is specific to a project, region, model, and version. Provisioned Throughput is assigned to a specific project-region-model-version combination. The same model called from a different region won't count against your Provisioned Throughput quota and won't be prioritized over on-demand requests.

docs.title: Context caching
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

Provisioned Throughput supports default context caching. However, Provisioned Throughput doesn't support caching requests using the Vertex AI API, which include retrieving information about a context cache using the Vertex AI API.

By default, Google automatically caches inputs to reduce cost and latency. For the Gemini 1.5 Flash and Gemini 1.5 Pro models, cached tokens are charged at a 75% discount relative to standard input tokens when a cache hit occurs. For Provisioned Throughput, the discount is applied through a reduced burndown rate.

For example, Gemini 1.5 Pro has the following burndown rates for input text tokens and cached tokens:

  • 1 input text token = 1 token
  • 1 input cached text token = 0.25 tokens

Sending 1,000 input tokens to this model would result in a burndown of your Provisioned Throughput by 1,000 input tokens per second. However, if you send 1,000 cached tokens to Gemini 1.5 Pro, this results in a burndown of your Provisioned Throughput by 250 tokens per second.

Note that this can lead to higher throughput for similar queries where the tokens aren't cached and the cache discount isn't applied.

To view the burndown rates for models supported in Provisioned Throughput, see Supported models and burndown rates.

docs.title: Example of estimating your Provisioned Throughput needs
docs.text:
To estimate your Provisioned Throughput needs, you can use the estimation tool in the Google Cloud console. The following example illustrates the process of estimating the amount of Provisioned Throughput for your model. The region isn't considered in the estimation calculations.

flowchart LR
    A[Gather requirements] --> B[Calculate throughput]
    B --> C[Calculate GSUs]

click A "#gather-requirements"
click B "#calculate-throughput"
click C "#calculate-gsus"

This table provides the burndown rates for gemini-1.0-pro that you can use to follow the example.

Model Throughput per GSU Units Minimum GSU purchase increment Burndown rates Gemini 1.0 Pro 3,360 Tokens 1 1 input text token = 1 token 1 input image token = 1 token 1 input video token = 1 token 1 input audio token = 7 tokens 1 output text token = 4 tokens Example: Estimate your Provisioned Throughput needs

Step 1: Gather your requirements

In this example, your requirement is to support 10 queries per second (QPS) of a query with an input of 1,000 text tokens and 500 audio tokens, to receive an output of 300 text tokens using gemini-1.0-pro. To calculate your throughput, refer to the burndown rates for your selected model.

Step 2: Calculate your throughput

  1. Multiply your inputs by the burndown rates to arrive at total input tokens: 1,000 * (1 token per input text token) + 500 * (7 tokens per input audio token) = 4,500 burndown adjusted input tokens per query.
  2. Multiply your outputs by the burndown rates to arrive at total output tokens: 300 * (4 tokens per output text token) = 1,200 burndown adjusted output tokens per query.
  3. Add your totals together: 4,500 burndown adjusted input tokens + 1,200 burndown adjusted output tokens = 5,700 total tokens per query.
  4. Multiply the total number of tokens by the QPS to arrive at total throughput per second: 5,700 total tokens per query * 10 QPS = 57,000 total tokens per second.

Step 3: Calculate your GSUs

  1. The GSUs are the total tokens per second divided by per-second throughput per GSU from the burndown table. 57,000 total tokens per second ÷ 3,360 per-second throughput per GSU = 16.96 GSUs.
  2. The minimum GSU purchase increment for gemini-1.0-pro is 1, so you'll need 17 GSUs to support your workload.

docs.title: Provisioned Throughput overview
docs.text:
This page explains what Provisioned Throughput is and helps you decide if it's the right choice for your generative AI applications on Vertex AI.

Provisioned Throughput is a fixed-cost, fixed-term subscription that reserves processing capacity for supported generative AI models. To reserve your throughput, you must specify the model and the available locations where the model runs.

docs.title: Consumption models
docs.text:
Vertex AI offers two consumption models for using generative AI models: Provisioned Throughput and Pay-as-you-go. The following table compares the two models to help you choose the best option for your workload.

Feature Provisioned Throughput Pay-as-you-go (On-demand) Cost Model Fixed-cost, fixed-term subscription for predictable billing. Pay only for what you use. Performance Reserved, consistent high throughput for stable performance. Throughput is based on a dynamic, shared quota. Performance can vary with demand. Best for Real-time production applications, such as chatbots and agents, and critical workloads that require consistently high throughput. Development, testing, and applications with variable or unpredictable traffic. Cost Control Provides deterministic costs with control over overages. Costs scale directly with usage.

docs.title: When to choose Provisioned Throughput
docs.text:
Consider using Provisioned Throughput if your use case meets one or more of the following criteria:

  • You are building real-time generative AI production applications, such as chatbots and agents.
  • Your critical workloads consistently require high throughput. Throughput measurement depends on the model.
  • You want to provide a consistent and predictable experience for users of your applications.
  • You want deterministic generative AI costs by paying a fixed price, with control over overages.

docs.title: Purchase Provisioned Throughput
docs.text: This page provides details to consider before subscribing to Provisioned Throughput, the permissions you must have to place or to view a Provisioned Throughput order, and the instructions for placing and viewing your orders.

docs.title: What to consider before purchasing
docs.text:
To help you decide whether you want to purchase Provisioned Throughput, consider the following:

  • Your purchase is a commitment for the entire term and cannot be canceled mid-term. If you accidentally purchase a commitment or there's a problem with your configuration, contact your Google Cloud account representative for assistance.

  • You can configure your subscription to auto-renew. When you submit your order, you can choose to auto-renew your subscription at the end of its term. You can cancel the auto-renewal up to 30 days before the start of the next term. Monthly subscriptions can be configured to renew automatically, but weekly terms do not support automatic renewal. For more information, see Change a Provisioned Throughput order.

  • You can change your auto-renewal behavior, model, model version, or region with notice. After your order is active, you can modify your existing order to change your auto-renewal behavior, model, or model version using the Google Cloud console. Model changes are limited to a specific publisher (e.g., you can switch between Google's Gemini models, but not from a Google model to an Anthropic model). To change your region, contact your Google Cloud account representative. All changes are processed on a best-effort basis and are typically fulfilled within 10 business days.

  • Overage is billed as pay-as-you-go by default. If your throughput exceeds your purchased amount, overages are processed and billed as standard pay-as-you-go. You can control overages on a per-request basis. For more information, see Use Provisioned Throughput.

For information about pricing, see Provisioned Throughput pricing.

docs.title: Place a Provisioned Throughput order
docs.text:
This section outlines the workflow for purchasing Provisioned Throughput. Orders are processed based on the size of the order and available capacity. Depending on the number of GSUs requested, it might take from a few minutes to a few weeks to process your order.

flowchart LR
    A[Prerequisites] --> B[Navigate to Provisioned Throughput]
    B --> C[Configure order]
    C --> D[Review and confirm]

click A "#prerequisites"
click B "#navigate-to-provisioned-throughput"
click C "#configure-order"
click D "#review-and-confirm"
Prerequisites

  • Imagen access: Some Imagen capabilities might not be publicly available. To learn more, see Restricted GA and Preview features.
  • MedLM access: Before you place an order to use MedLM-large-1.5, contact your Google Cloud account representative to request access.
  • Quota adjustment: If you expect your queries per minute (QPM) to exceed 30,000, request a quota adjustment for your default Vertex AI system quota using the following information:
    • Service: The Vertex AI API.
    • Name: Online prediction requests per minute per region
    • Service type: A quota.
    • Dimensions: The region where you ordered Provisioned Throughput.
    • Value: Your chosen online-prediction traffic limit.
Place your order

1. Navigate to the Provisioned Throughput page

In the Google Cloud console, go to the Provisioned Throughput page.

Go to Provisioned Throughput

To start a new order, click New order.

2. Configure your order

  • Enter an Order name.
  • Select the Model.
  • Select the Region.
  • Enter the Number of generative AI scale units (GSUs) that you want to purchase.
Use the Generative AI scale unit estimation tool (Optional)

You can use the estimation tool to help determine the number of GSUs you need.

  1. Click Estimation tool.
  2. Select your Model.
  3. Based on the selected model, enter the details to estimate the number of GSUs needed.
    • For Gemini 2.5 models, enter the estimated queries per second and tokens per query for text, image, video, and audio inputs and outputs.
    • For Gemini 2.0 models, enter the estimated queries per second and tokens per query for text, image, video, and audio inputs and outputs.
    • For Imagen models, enter the queries per second and output images per query.
  4. To use the calculated value in your order, click Use calculated.
  • Select your Term: 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, or 1 year.
  • Optional: Select the Start date and time for your term. > Preview > > You can provide a start date and time within two weeks from when you place the order. If you don't specify a start time, the order is processed as soon as capacity is available. Requested start times are processed on a best-effort basis.
  • In the Renewal list, specify whether you want to automatically renew the order at the end of the term. This option is available for terms of 1 month or longer.

3. Review and confirm

  • Click Continue.
  • In the Summary section, review the price and throughput estimates for your order.
  • Read the terms listed and linked in the form.
  • To finalize your order, click Confirm.

It can take from a few minutes to a few weeks to process an order. After the order is processed, its status in the Google Cloud console changes to Active, and billing begins.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Change a Provisioned Throughput order
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

You can modify your Provisioned Throughput orders through the Google Cloud console. The actions you can take depend on the status of your order. Modifying orders is a Preview feature and is only available for online orders placed through the console. For changes to offline orders, contact your Google Cloud account representative for assistance.

Order status Available actions Pending review Cancel the order. Approved No modifications are possible while awaiting activation. Active Increase GSUs, enable or disable auto-renewal, or change the model or model version (with restrictions). Pending reviewApprovedActive

If your order is pending review, you can cancel it. If you need to make other changes, cancel the pending order and place a new one. Each model can only have one pending order or pending order revision at a time.

To cancel your pending order:

  1. Go to the Provisioned Throughput page.
  2. Select the Region where your pending order is located.
  3. Click the Order ID for the order that you want to cancel to go to the Order details page.
  4. Click Cancel.
  5. In the confirmation dialog, click Cancel Order.

The order is awaiting activation. You can't make changes to your order at this time.

You can modify an active order if it does not expire in the next five days or if it is set to renew automatically. You can perform the following actions:

  • Increase GSUs on existing orders.
  • Enable or disable automatic renewals.
  • Change the model or model version.

Changes to the model or model version modify the existing order while keeping the same subscription end date.

To change your active order:

  1. Navigate to the Provisioned Throughput page.
  2. Find your active order and do one of the following:
    • In the Actions column, click the more_vert menu and select Edit.
    • Click the Order ID to go to the Order details page, then click Edit.
  3. Make your desired changes and confirm.

docs.title: Check order status
docs.text:
After you submit your Provisioned Throughput order, the order status appears as one of the following:

  • Pending review: Your order has been placed and is awaiting review and approval, which depends on available capacity.
  • Approved: Your order has been approved and is awaiting activation. You can't make changes after the order is approved.
  • Active: Your order has been activated, and billing has started.
  • Expired: Your order has expired.

docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

The following is supported for Google models that support supervised fine-tuning:

  • Provisioned Throughput can be applied to both base models and supervised fine-tuned versions of those base models.
  • Supervised fine-tuned model endpoints and their corresponding base model count towards the same Provisioned Throughput quota.

For example, Provisioned Throughput purchased for gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001 for a specific project prioritizes requests that are made from supervised fine-tuned versions of gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001 created within that project. Use the appropriate header to control traffic behavior.

docs.title: Use Provisioned Throughput
docs.text: This page explains how Provisioned Throughput works, how to control overages or bypass Provisioned Throughput, and how to monitor usage.

docs.title: How Provisioned Throughput works
docs.text: This section explains how Provisioned Throughput works by using quota checking through the quota enforcement period.

docs.title: Provisioned Throughput quota checking
docs.text:
Your Provisioned Throughput maximum quota is a multiple of the number of generative AI scale units (GSUs) purchased and the throughput per GSU. It's checked each time you make a request within your quota enforcement period, which is how frequently the maximum Provisioned Throughput quota is enforced.

At the time a request is received, the true response size is unknown. Because we prioritize speed of response for real-time applications, Provisioned Throughput estimates the output token size. If the initial estimate exceeds the available Provisioned Throughput maximum quota, the request is processed as pay-as-you-go. Otherwise, it is processed as Provisioned Throughput. This is done by comparing the initial estimate to your Provisioned Throughput maximum quota.

When the response is generated and the true output token size is known, actual usage and quota are reconciled by adding the difference between the estimate and the actual usage to your available Provisioned Throughput quota amount.

docs.title: Provisioned Throughput quota enforcement period
docs.text:
For gemini-2.0-flash-lite and gemini-2.0-flash models, the quota enforcement period can take up to 30 seconds and is subject to change. This means that you might temporarily experience prioritized traffic that exceeds your quota amount on a per-second basis in some cases, but you shouldn't exceed your quota on a 30-second basis. These periods are based on the Vertex AI internal clock time and are independent of when requests are made.

For example, if you purchase one GSU of gemini-2.0-flash-001, then you should expect 3,360 tokens per second of always-on throughput. On average, you can't exceed 100,800 tokens on a 30-second basis, which is calculated using the following formula:

3,360 tokens per second * 30 seconds = 100,800 tokens

If, in a day, you submitted only one request that consumed 8,000 tokens in a second, it might still be processed as a Provisioned Throughput request, even though you exceeded your 3,360 tokens per second limit at the time of the request. This is because the request didn't exceed the threshold of 100,800 tokens per 30 seconds.

docs.title: Control overages or bypass Provisioned Throughput
docs.text:
Before you send requests, you need to decide how to handle traffic that exceeds your purchased throughput. You can allow overages to be billed as pay-as-you-go, block overages entirely, or bypass your provisioned capacity for specific requests.

The following table compares the available options.

Method X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type Header Description Best for... Default (Spillover) Not set Requests use Provisioned Throughput. If the limit is exceeded, overage traffic is processed using on-demand capacity and billed at the pay-as-you-go rate. Production applications that need to handle traffic spikes without returning errors. Provisioned Throughput Only dedicated Requests only use Provisioned Throughput. If the limit is exceeded, requests return an error 429. Cost-sensitive applications where avoiding on-demand charges is critical. Pay-as-you-go Only (Bypass) shared Requests bypass the Provisioned Throughput order and are sent directly to on-demand, pay-as-you-go capacity. Development, testing, or non-critical workloads that shouldn't consume your provisioned capacity.

docs.title: Set request behavior with code examples
docs.text:
You can control the request behavior by setting the X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type HTTP header in your API calls.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

Python SDKREST

Install the SDK

pip install --upgrade google-genai

To learn more, see the SDK reference documentation.

Set environment variables

# Replace the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` values
# with appropriate values for your project.
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=True

Initialize the client with a request header

The following example shows how to set the header to shared to bypass Provisioned Throughput. To use only Provisioned Throughput, set the value to dedicated.

from google import genai
from google.genai.types import HttpOptions

client = genai.Client(
    http_options=HttpOptions(
        api_version="v1",
        headers={
            # Options:
            # - "dedicated": Use Provisioned Throughput only
            # - "shared": Use pay-as-you-go only
            # If not set, defaults to spillover behavior.
            "X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type": "shared"
        },
    )
)
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="How does AI work?",
)
print(response.text)
# Example response:
# Okay, let's break down how AI works. It's a broad field, so I'll focus on the ...
#
# Here's a simplified overview:
# ...

After you set up your environment, you can send a request with the X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type header.

The following example shows how to set the header to dedicated to use only Provisioned Throughput. To bypass Provisioned Throughput, set the value to shared.

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type: dedicated" \ # Options: dedicated, shared
  $URL \
  -d '{"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Hello."}]}]}'

docs.title: Monitor Provisioned Throughput
docs.text:
Preview

This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions.

You can monitor your Provisioned Throughput usage using metrics in Cloud Monitoring. The following workflow outlines the monitoring process.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Monitor Provisioned Throughput
        A[View Dashboards]
        B[Enable Alerts]
    end

    click A "#dashboards"
    click B "#alerting"

You can self-monitor your Provisioned Throughput usage using a set of metrics that are measured on the aiplatform.googleapis.com/PublisherModel resource type.

Provisioned Throughput traffic monitoring is a public Preview feature.

Dimensions

You can filter on metrics using the following dimensions:

Dimension Values type input output request_type dedicated: Traffic is processed using Provisioned Throughput. spillover: Traffic is processed as pay-as-you-go quota after you exceed your Provisioned Throughput quota. shared: If Provisioned Throughput is active, then traffic is processed as pay-as-you-go quota using the shared HTTP header. If Provisioned Throughput isn't active, then traffic is processed as pay-as-you-go, by default.

Path prefix

The path prefix for a metric is aiplatform.googleapis.com/publisher/online_serving.

For example, the full path for the /consumed_throughput metric is aiplatform.googleapis.com/publisher/online_serving/consumed_throughput.

Metrics

The following Cloud Monitoring metrics are available on the aiplatform.googleapis.com/PublisherModel resource for the Gemini models. Use the dedicated request types to filter for Provisioned Throughput usage.

Metric Display name Description /dedicated_gsu_limit Limit (GSU) Dedicated limit in GSUs. Use this metric to understand your Provisioned Throughput maximum quota in GSUs. /tokens Tokens Input and output token count distribution. /token_count Token count Accumulated input and output token count. /consumed_token_throughput Token throughput Throughput usage, which accounts for the burndown rate in tokens and incorporates quota reconciliation. See Provisioned Throughput quota checking. Use this metric to understand how your Provisioned Throughput quota was used. /dedicated_token_limit Limit (tokens per second) Dedicated limit in tokens per second. Use this metric to understand your Provisioned Throughput maximum quota for token-based models. /characters Characters Input and output character count distribution. /character_count Character count Accumulated input and output character count. /consumed_throughput Character throughput Throughput usage, which accounts for the burndown rate in characters and incorporates quota reconciliation Provisioned Throughput quota checking. Use this metric to understand how your Provisioned Throughput quota was used. For token-based models, this metric is equivalent to the throughput consumed in tokens multiplied by 4. /dedicated_character_limit Limit (characters per second) Dedicated limit in characters per second. Use this metric to understand your Provisioned Throughput maximum quota for character-based models. /model_invocation_count Model invocation count Number of model invocations (prediction requests). /model_invocation_latencies Model invocation latencies Model invocation latencies (prediction latencies). /first_token_latencies First token latencies Duration from request received to first token returned.

Anthropic models also have a filter for Provisioned Throughput but only for tokens/token_count.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
View monitoring dashboards

Default monitoring dashboards for Provisioned Throughput provide metrics that let you better understand your usage and Provisioned Throughput utilization. To access the dashboards, do the following:

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Provisioned Throughput page.

    Go to Provisioned Throughput

  2. To view the Provisioned Throughput utilization of each model across your orders, select the Utilization summary tab.

  3. Select a model from the Provisioned Throughput utilization by model table to see more metrics specific to the selected model.

Limitations of the dashboard

The dashboard might display unexpected results, especially for fluctuating traffic that's either spiky or infrequent (for example, less than 1 query per second). The following reasons might contribute to those results:

  • Time ranges that are larger than 12 hours can lead to a less accurate representation of the quota enforcement period. Throughput metrics and their derivatives, such as utilization, display averages across alignment periods that are based on the selected time range. When the time range expands, each alignment period also expands. The alignment period expands across the calculation of the average usage. Because quota enforcement is calculated at a sub-minute level, setting the time range to a period of 12 hours or less results in minute-level data that is more comparable to the actual quota enforcement period. For more information on alignment periods, see Alignment: within-series regularization. For more information about time ranges, see Regularizing time intervals.
  • If multiple requests were submitted at the same time, monitoring aggregations might impact your ability to filter down to specific requests.
  • Provisioned Throughput throttles traffic when a request was made but reports usage metrics after the quota is reconciled.
  • Provisioned Throughput quota enforcement periods are independent from and might not align with monitoring aggregation periods or request-or-response periods.
  • If no errors occurred, you might see an error message within the error rate chart. For example, An error occurred requesting data. One or more resources could not be found.

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text:
After alerting is enabled, set default alerts to help you manage your traffic usage.

Enable recommended alerts

To enable alerts in the dashboard, do the following:

  1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Provisioned Throughput page.

    Go to Provisioned Throughput

  2. To view the Provisioned Throughput utilization of each model across your orders, select the Utilization summary tab.

  3. Select Recommended alerts, and the following alerts display:

    • Provisioned Throughput Usage Reached Limit
    • Provisioned Throughput Utilization Exceeded 80%
    • Provisioned Throughput Utilization Exceeded 90%

  4. Check the alerts that help you manage your traffic.

View more alert details

To view more information about alerts, do the following:

  1. Go to the Integrations page.

    Go to Integrations

  2. Enter vertex into the Filter field and press Enter. Google Vertex AI appears.

  3. To view more information, click View details. The Google Vertex AI details pane displays.

  4. Select Alerts tab, and you can select an Alert Policy template.

docs.title: Fine-tune RAG transformations
docs.text: When you ingest documents, Vertex AI RAG Engine automatically runs a series of transformations to process and chunk your data before it's indexed. You can fine-tune this process by adjusting parameters to optimize retrieval quality for your specific use case.

docs.title: RAG transformation parameters
docs.text:
You can control how your data is prepared for indexing by using the following parameters:

Parameter Description chunk_size When documents are ingested, they are split into chunks. This parameter specifies the size of each chunk in tokens. The default is 1,024 tokens. chunk_overlap To improve retrieval quality and maintain context, consecutive chunks are created with a certain amount of overlap. This parameter specifies the overlap size in tokens. The default is 200 tokens.

docs.title: How to choose chunk size and overlap
docs.text:
Selecting the right chunk_size and chunk_overlap is a trade-off between precision and context.

  • Smaller chunk_size: Creates more granular, focused chunks.

    • Pros: Embeddings are more precise, making it ideal for retrieving specific facts, definitions, or answers to highly targeted questions.
    • Cons: May lose the broader context surrounding the information, which can be crucial for more complex or summarization-based queries.

  • Larger chunk_size: Retains more context within each chunk.

    • Pros: Better for summarization tasks and questions that require understanding a larger narrative or argument.
    • Cons: The embedding for a large chunk might generalize the content, potentially "diluting" specific details and making it harder to retrieve precise facts.

The chunk_overlap helps ensure that a sentence or concept isn't awkwardly split between two chunks, which could cause it to be missed during retrieval. A larger overlap increases redundancy but reduces the chance of losing information at chunk boundaries.

docs.title: Use-case examples
docs.text:
• For technical Q&A: If your documents are technical manuals and your users ask specific questions like "What does error code 503 mean?", a smaller chunk_size (e.g., 256 or 512) is often better. This isolates specific details and improves the precision of search results.

  • For document summarization: If your goal is to summarize long reports or legal documents, a larger chunk_size (e.g., 1024 or 2048) is more effective. This ensures that each chunk contains enough context for the model to generate a coherent and comprehensive summary.

docs.title: Use Document AI layout parser with Vertex AI RAG Engine
docs.text:
This page explains how to use the Document AI layout parser when importing files into Vertex AI RAG Engine.

Note

The VPC-SC security control is supported by RAG Engine. Data residency, CMEK, and AXT security controls aren't supported.

docs.title: Document AI
docs.text: Document AI is a document-processing platform that takes unstructured data from documents and transforms it into structured data suitable for analysis and storage. It uses generative AI to help you create scalable, end-to-end, cloud-based document processing applications without requiring specialized machine-learning expertise.

docs.title: Document AI layout parser
docs.text:
The layout parser is a feature of Document AI that extracts content elements from a document, such as text, tables, and lists. It then creates context-aware chunks that preserve the document's original structure. By considering the document's layout during the chunking process, the parser improves semantic coherence and reduces noise, which enhances information retrieval for generative AI applications.

For more information on supported file types, see Layout detection per file type.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The following limitations apply when using the layout parser with the ImportRagFiles API: * Maximum input file size is 20 MB for all file types. * Maximum of 500 pages per PDF file.

Standard Document AI quotas and pricing apply.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the workflow for integrating the Document AI layout parser with RAG Engine.

    B --> C[Import files];

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Expand to see the prerequisites

1. Enable the Document AI API

You must enable the Document AI API for your project. For more information, see the Service Usage documentation.

Enable the Document AI API

2. Create and enable a layout parser

You need a layout parser processor to parse your documents.

  • Create a layout parser by following the instructions in Creating and managing processors. The processor type name is LAYOUT_PARSER_PROCESSOR.
  • Enable the layout parser by following the instructions in Enable a processor.

3. Prepare your RAG corpus

  • If you don't have a RAG corpus, create one. For an example, see Create a RAG corpus.
  • If you have an existing RAG corpus, note that files previously imported without a layout parser will not be automatically re-processed. To apply the layout parser to these files, you must first delete them and then re-import them with the parser enabled. For an example, see Delete a RAG file.

docs.title: Choose an integration method
docs.text:
You can import files with the layout parser using either the Google Cloud console for a UI-driven approach or the Vertex AI API for programmatic control. The following table provides a comparison to help you decide which method is best for your use case.

Feature Google Cloud console Vertex AI API (Python/REST) Use Case Ideal for quick setup, one-time uploads, and exploring features through a visual interface. Best for programmatic integration, automating ingestion pipelines, and building custom applications. Control Guided setup with pre-defined options for chunking and parsing. Full programmatic control over all import parameters, including chunking and parser configuration. Effort Low effort, requires manual steps through the UI. Higher effort, requires writing code to interact with the API.

docs.title: Import files using the layout parser
Use your RAG corpus
docs.text:
Once your files are imported and processed with the layout parser, your RAG corpus is ready to be used for information retrieval and generation.

  • Retrieval: When a user provides a query, the retrieval component searches the corpus to find relevant information. For an example, see Retrieval query.
  • Prediction: The prediction component uses the retrieved contexts to generate a grounded response. For an example, see Generation.

docs.title: Use the LLM parser
docs.text:
Preview

Some of the RAG features are Preview offerings, subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" of the Google Cloud Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA products and features may have limited support, and changes to Pre-GA products and features may not be compatible with other Pre-GA versions. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. Further, by using the Gemini API on Vertex AI, you agree to the Generative AI Preview terms and conditions (Preview Terms).

This page explains how to use the Vertex AI RAG Engine LLM parser.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine uses LLMs for document parsing. LLMs have the ability to effectively process documents in the following ways:

  • Understand and interpret semantic content across various formats.
  • Retrieve relevant document chunks.
  • Extract meaningful information from documents.
  • Identify relevant sections in documents.
  • Accurately summarize complex documents.
  • Understand and interact with visuals.
  • Extract data from charts and diagrams.
  • Describe images.
  • Understand relationships between charts and text.
  • Provide more contextually rich and accurate responses.

The capabilities of the Vertex AI RAG Engine significantly improves the quality of generated responses.

docs.title: Supported models and file types
docs.text:
The LLM parser only supports Gemini models. If you have the RAG API enabled, you have access to the supported models. For a list of supported generation models, see Generative models.

The following file types are supported by the LLM parser:

  • application/pdf
  • image/png
  • image/jpeg
  • image/webp
  • image/heic
  • image/heif

docs.title: Security controls
docs.text: The VPC-SC security control is supported by RAG Engine. Data residency, CMEK, and AXT security controls aren't supported.

docs.title: Pricing and quotas
docs.text:
For pricing details, see Vertex AI pricing. For applicable quotas, see Request quotas.

The LLM parser calls Gemini models to parse your documents. This creates additional costs, which are charged to your project. The cost can be roughly estimated using this formula:

cost = number_of_document_files * average_pages_per_document * (average_input_tokens * input_token_pricing_of_selected_model + average_output_tokens * output_token_pricing_of_selected_model)

For example, you have 1,000 PDF files, and each PDF file has 50 pages. The average PDF page has 500 tokens, and we need an additional 100 tokens for prompting. The average output is 100 tokens.

Gemini 1.5 Flash is used in your configuration for parsing, and it costs $0.075 for 1M input tokens and $0.3 for output text tokens.

Note: This example is for educational purposes on how to estimate your cost. It doesn't reflect the real cost you pay for every indexing request using the LLM parser.

cost = 1,000 * 50 * (600 * 0.075 / 1M + 100 * 0.3 / 1M) = 3.75

The cost is $3.75.

docs.title: How to import files with the LLM parser
docs.text:
This section shows how to import files from Cloud Storage or Google Drive and parse them using a specified Gemini model.

flowchart LR
    A[Prepare configuration] --> B[Import files];

click A "#prepare-configuration"
click B "#import-files"

Prepare configuration

Before making the import request, replace the following placeholder variables with your own values.

  • PROJECT_ID: The ID for your Google Cloud project.
  • LOCATION: The region where your request is processed (for example, us-central1).
  • RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE: The numeric ID of your corpus.
  • GCS_URI: The Cloud Storage URI of the files you want to import (for example, gs://my-bucket/my-files/).
  • GOOGLE_DRIVE_URI: The Google Drive URI of the files you want to import.
  • MODEL_NAME: The resource name of the model used for parsing. Format: projects/{project_id}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/{model_id}.
  • CUSTOM_PARSING_PROMPT: (Optional) A custom prompt for the LLM parser to use for parsing documents.
  • MAX_PARSING_REQUESTS_PER_MIN: (Optional) The maximum number of requests the job can make to the Vertex AI model per minute. For more information, see Generative AI on Vertex AI rate limits and the Quotas & System Limits page for your project to set an appropriate value.

Import files

Use the following samples to import your files.

Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with code snippets or setup, refer to the Troubleshooting Guide.

RESTPython 
curl -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
"https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE/ragFiles:import" -d '{
  "import_rag_files_config": {
    "gcs_source": {
      "uris":  ["GCS_URI", "GOOGLE_DRIVE_URI"]
    },
    "rag_file_chunking_config": {
      "chunk_size": 512,
      "chunk_overlap": 102
    },
    "rag_file_parsing_config": {
      "llm_parser": {
        "model_name": "MODEL_NAME",
        "custom_parsing_prompt": "CUSTOM_PARSING_PROMPT",
        "max_parsing_requests_per_min": "MAX_PARSING_REQUESTS_PER_MIN"
      }
    }
  }
}'

To learn how to install or update the Vertex AI SDK for Python, see Install the Vertex AI SDK for Python. For more information, see the Python API reference documentation.

from vertexai import rag
import vertexai

PROJECT_ID = "PROJECT_ID"
CORPUS_NAME = "RAG_CORPUS_RESOURCE"
LOCATION = "LOCATION"
MODEL_ID = "MODEL_ID"
MODEL_NAME = f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/locations/{LOCATION}/publishers/google/models/{MODEL_ID}"
MAX_PARSING_REQUESTS_PER_MIN = MAX_PARSING_REQUESTS_PER_MIN # Optional
CUSTOM_PARSING_PROMPT = "Your custom prompt" # Optional

PATHS = ["https://drive.google.com/file/123", "gs://my_bucket/my_files_dir"]

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project={PROJECT_ID}, location={LOCATION})

transformation_config = rag.TransformationConfig(
    chunking_config=rag.ChunkingConfig(
        chunk_size=1024, # Optional
        chunk_overlap=200, # Optional
    ),
)

llm_parser_config = rag.LlmParserConfig(
    model_name = MODEL_NAME,
    max_parsing_requests_per_min=MAX_PARSING_REQUESTS_PER_MIN, # Optional
    custom_parsing_prompt=CUSTOM_PARSING_PROMPT, # Optional
)

rag.import_files(
    CORPUS_NAME,
    PATHS,
    llm_parser=llm_parser_config,
    transformation_config=transformation_config,
)

docs.title: Customize the parsing prompt
docs.text:
The Vertex AI RAG Engine LLM parser uses a predefined, tuned prompt for parsing documents. However, if you have specialized documents that might not be suitable for a general prompt, you can specify a custom parsing prompt.

Prompt template table

The following table provides a prompt template to guide you in creating prompts that Vertex AI RAG Engine can use to parse your documents:

Instruction Template statement Example Specify role. You are a/an [Specify the role, such as a factual data extractor or an information retriever]. You are an information retriever. Specify task. Extract [Specify the type of information, such as factual statements, key data, or specific details] from the [Specify the document source, such as a document, text, article, image, table]. Extract key data from the sample.txt file. Explain how you want the LLM to generate the output according to your documents. Present each fact in a [Specify the output format, such as a structured list or text format], and link to its [Specify the source location, such as a page, paragraph, table, or row]. Present each fact in a structured list, and link to its sample page. Highlight what should be the focus of the LLM. Extract [Specify the key data types, such as the names, dates, numbers, attributes, or relationships] exactly as stated. Extract names and dates. Highlight what you want the LLM to avoid. [List the actions to avoid, such as analysis, interpretation, summarizing, inferring, or giving opinions]. Extract only what the document explicitly says. No giving opinions. Extract only what the document explicitly says.

General guidance

Follow these guidelines when writing your custom prompt:

  • Be specific: Clearly define the task and the type of information to be extracted.
  • Be detailed: Provide detailed instructions on output format, source attribution, and handling of different data structures.
  • Be constraining: Explicitly state what the AI should not do, such as analysis or interpretation.
  • Be clear: Use clear and directive language.
  • Be structured: Organize instructions logically using numbered lists or bullet points for readability.

docs.title: Parsing quality analysis
docs.text:
This table lists results from scenarios that customers ran using Vertex AI RAG Engine. The feedback shows that the LLM parser improves the quality of parsing documents.

Scenario Result Parsing information across slides and linking sections The LLM parser successfully linked section titles on one slide to the detailed information presented on subsequent slides. Understanding and extracting information from tables The LLM parser correctly related columns and headers within a large table to answer specific questions. Interpreting flowcharts The LLM parser was able to follow the logic of a flowchart and extract the correct sequence of actions and corresponding information. Extracting data from graphs The LLM parser could interpret different types of graphs, such as line graphs, and extract specific data points based on the query. Capturing relationships between headings and text The LLM parser, guided by the prompt, paid attention to heading structures and could retrieve all relevant information associated with a particular topic or section. Potential to overcome embedding limitations with prompt engineering While initially hampered by embedding model limitations in some use cases, additional experiments demonstrated that a well-crafted LLM parser prompt could potentially mitigate these issues and retrieve the correct information even when semantic understanding is challenging for the embedding model alone.

The LLM parser enhances the LLM's ability to understand and reason about the context within a document, which leads to more accurate and comprehensive responses.

You can manage your RAG corpuses using either the v1 (General Availability) or v1beta1 (Preview) version of the RAG API.

docs.title: Vertex AI RAG Engine overview
docs.text:
Vertex AI RAG Engine is a component of the Vertex AI Platform that facilitates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). It acts as a data framework for developing large language model (LLM) applications that are augmented with your organization's private data.

A common challenge with LLMs is their inability to access private, up-to-date information. By connecting an LLM to your data sources, RAG Engine enriches the model's context, which helps reduce hallucinations and enables it to provide more accurate, factually grounded answers.

To get started, try the quickstart or go directly to the console.

Try the RAG quickstart for Python Try Vertex AI RAG Engine

docs.title: How RAG Engine works
docs.text:
The core of RAG Engine is a process that finds relevant data from your specified sources, synthesizes it, and uses it to provide a more informed answer to a user's query.

flowchart LR
    A[Data ingestion] --> B[Data transformation]
    B --> C[Embedding]
    C --> D[Data indexing]
    D --> E[Retrieval]
    E --> F[Generation]

click A "#data-ingestion"
click B "#data-transformation"
click C "#embedding"
click D "#data-indexing"
click E "#retrieval"
click F "#generation"
The RAG process in Vertex AI RAG Engine.

The following steps describe the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) process.

The RAG process

1. Data ingestion

Intake data from various sources, such as local files, Cloud Storage, and Google Drive.

2. Data transformation

Convert the raw data in preparation for indexing. For example, data is split into smaller, manageable chunks. For more information, see Fine-tune RAG transformations.

3. Embedding

Create numerical representations (embeddings) of the text chunks. These numbers capture the semantic meaning and context of the text. Similar or related text will have similar embeddings, meaning they are close to each other in the vector space. For more information, see Get text embeddings.

4. Data indexing

Vertex AI RAG Engine creates an index, called a corpus, from the embeddings. The index structures the knowledge base to be optimized for fast and efficient searching, similar to a detailed table of contents for a massive reference book.

5. Retrieval

When a user asks a question or provides a prompt, the retrieval component in RAG Engine searches the indexed corpus to find information that is semantically relevant to the query.

6. Generation

The retrieved information is added as context to the original user query. This combined input is then sent to the generative model, which uses the context as a guide to generate a factually grounded and relevant response.

docs.title: RAG quickstart for Python
docs.text:

docs.title: Perform RAG tasks
docs.text:
After setting up your environment, you can use the Vertex AI SDK to perform RAG tasks. You can either retrieve context directly from your RAG corpus or use the corpus to augment the responses of a generative model.

Direct context retrievalAugment generation with a model

This approach is useful when you only need to retrieve relevant text chunks from your documents based on a query. The following code demonstrates how to create a RagCorpus, import files, and perform a retrieval query.

from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
# BUCKET_URI = "gs://your-bucket/your-folder"  # Cloud Storage URI
#
# RAG_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME = "rag-corpus-1"
# RAG_FILES_PATHS = [BUCKET_URI] # Supports Google Cloud Storage and Google Drive Links

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Create RagCorpus
rag_corpus = rag.create_corpus(
    display_name=RAG_CORPUS_DISPLAY_NAME,
)

# Import Files to the RagCorpus
# You can supply a list of local file paths, GCS URIs, or Google Drive URIs.
response = rag.import_files(
    rag_corpus.name,
    RAG_FILES_PATHS,
    # Optional
    chunk_size=512,
    chunk_overlap=100,
)

# Direct context retrieval
response = rag.retrieval_query(
    rag_resources=[
        rag.RagResource(
            rag_corpus=rag_corpus.name,
            # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
            # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
        )
    ],
    text="What is RAG and why it is helpful?",
    # Optional:
    top_k=3,
)
print(response)

This approach integrates your RAG corpus with a generative model (like Gemini) to provide contextually grounded responses. The corpus is converted into a Tool that the model can use to find relevant information before generating an answer.

from vertexai import rag
from vertexai.generative_models import GenerativeModel, Tool
import vertexai

# This section assumes you have already created a RagCorpus
# and have the `rag_corpus` object from the "Direct context retrieval" tab.

# TODO(developer): Update and un-comment below lines if you haven't already
# PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id"
#
# And make sure you have a `rag_corpus` object. For example:
# rag_corpus = rag.get_corpus("projects/your-project-id/locations/us-central1/ragCorpora/123456789")

# Initialize Vertex AI API once per session
vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location="us-central1")

# Create a RAG retrieval tool
rag_retrieval_tool = Tool.from_retrieval(
    retrieval=rag.Retrieval(
        source=rag.VertexRagStore(
            rag_resources=[
                rag.RagResource(
                    rag_corpus=rag_corpus.name,  # Currently only 1 corpus is allowed.
                    # Optional: supply IDs from `rag.list_files()`.
                    # rag_file_ids=["rag-file-1", "rag-file-2", ...],
                )
            ],
        ),
    )
)

# Create a Gemini model instance
rag_model = GenerativeModel(
    model_name="gemini-1.0-pro", tools=[rag_retrieval_tool]
)

# Generate response
response = rag_model.generate_content("What is RAG and why it is helpful?")
print(response.text)
# Example response:
#   RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
#   It's a technique used in AI to enhance the quality of responses
# ...

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
To avoid incurring unnecessary charges to your Google Cloud account, delete the resources you created for this tutorial. The primary resource to clean up is the RagCorpus.

# This section assumes you have the `rag_corpus` object from the previous steps.
rag.delete_corpus(name=rag_corpus.name)

print(f"Deleted RagCorpus: {rag_corpus.name}")

docs.title: Generative AI on Vertex AI quotas and system limits
docs.text: This page explains the consumption and quota models for Generative AI on Vertex AI services. It also provides specific quotas and limits by region and model, and shows you how to view and manage your quotas in the Google Cloud console.

docs.title: Consumption and quota models
docs.text:
There are two ways to consume generative AI services: pay-as-you-go (PayGo), where you pay for what you use, or Provisioned Throughput, where you pay a fixed price in advance for dedicated capacity.

Feature Pay-as-you-go (PayGo) Provisioned Throughput Pricing Pay for usage on-demand. Pay in advance for a fixed term (e.g., one hour). Capacity Capacity is shared and subject to availability. Capacity is reserved exclusively for your project. Performance Throughput and latency can vary based on overall demand. Predictable and consistent throughput and latency. Use Case Ideal for development, testing, and applications with variable or unpredictable traffic. Recommended for production applications requiring high availability and predictable performance.

If you're using PayGo, your usage is subject to one of two quota systems, depending on the model.

Quota System Description Key Feature Standard Quota A traditional quota system where a fixed number of requests per minute (RPM) is allocated to each project and region. Requires you to monitor usage and request quota increases if you exceed your limit. Dynamic Shared Quota (DSQ) A dynamic system that distributes available PayGo capacity among all customers for a specific model and region. Eliminates the need to set or request quota increases. There are no user-managed quotas with DSQ.
